Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the annual Firm Element needs analysis and the fitness-and-propriety file for every registered officer, director and principal of the broker-dealer distributing variable annuities; HR Business Partner supplies the appointment trigger, Employment Counsel clears adverse findings

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA Rule 1240(b) (Firm Element) plus Rules 1210/1220 registration categories re-read in the FINRA online rulebook at the start of each needs-analysis cycle, together with Rule 3110(e), FINRA By-Laws Article III Section 3 and the Exchange Act 3(a)(39) statutory disqualification definition; Rule 2211 and 2210(d)(1) drive the variable-product content standards taught

In-scope processes.value: Officer/director/principal appointment (nomination to registration to fitness assessment) and the calendar-year Firm Element cycle covering every registered person who sells, recommends or supervises variable annuities and variable life

In-scope systems.value: Firm Element curricula assigned, delivered and completion-tracked in the LMS; fitness questionnaires and screening reports held in the HRIS officer file; registration status read from CRD via FINRA Gateway

Compliance procedure documented.value: Fitness & Propriety and Firm Element Training Procedure — appointment questionnaire, CRD/BrokerCheck and criminal/credit screening, statutory-disqualification review, annual needs analysis, written training plan, delivery and completion chase

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Employment Counsel concurrence; re-approved each August before the needs analysis opens and on any FINRA Regulatory Notice amending Rule 1240 or the registration rules

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Firm Element plan written and delivery complete by December 31 of the calendar year; Form U4 amendment for a newly appointed officer within 30 days of the firm learning of the fact; MC-400 eligibility filing before a statutorily disqualified person acts in any registered capacity

Deadline reminders configured.value: LMS reminder mails at T-90, T-60 and T-30 days to December 31 for every incomplete Firm Element assignment; HRIS workflow alerts on day 10, 20 and 25 of the 30-day U4 amendment clock, escalating to the Head of Compliance on day 25

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Needs analysis, written training plan, courseware versions, per-person completion extracts, fitness questionnaires and screening reports retained 6 years (first 3 easily accessible) per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4; officer fitness files kept for the term of office plus 3 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any registered person past December 31 without Firm Element completion, and any officer acting before the fitness assessment closes, is raised as an exception with root cause, a registration/production restriction and a dated remediation plan

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs every completed fitness assessment for an officer or director and every Firm Element non-completion remediation before the restriction is lifted

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: All registered persons on the CRD roster at December 31 who fall inside the Firm Element covered-person definition, plus every officer, director and principal appointment or re-appointment effected during the calendar year

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on an officer or principal acting before a completed fitness assessment; Firm Element completion must reach 100% of covered persons by December 31 — any incomplete person is a fail and an incomplete rate above 2% escalates to the Audit Committee

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Obligation is annual with a per-appointment trigger; the test runs each January over the closed calendar year, with a quarterly spot check of that quarter's appointments so a mid-year gap is not discovered twelve months late

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have built the needs analysis, authored or delivered any Firm Element course, or performed any sampled fitness assessment

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Firm Element and fitness-assessment workpaper (roster reconciliation, sample list with seed, re-performance notes, exception log) filed in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C09 and the test year

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Needs analysis, written training plan, courseware index and per-person completion report plus officer fitness files, packaged as a Rule 1240(b) cycle exam response within 5 business days of a FINRA request

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the FINRA exam and Rule 8210 request response; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of untrained covered persons or unassessed officers before it leaves the firm

checklist.step: Open a fitness file when an officer, director or principal is nominated
actions: In Workday open Recruiting or Business Processes and filter for positions flagged 'Registered officer / principal' or 'Board appointment'.

Take from the Corporate Secretary the nomination memo naming the person, the office (CEO, CCO, FinOp, General Securities Principal, Investment Company and Variable Contracts Principal) and the intended effective date.
Raise an HRIS case named <surname>-fitness-<effective date> and set the target close date at 5 business days before the effective date.
Notify the Compliance Analyst and the Producer Licensing Coordinator through the case so screening and CRD work start the same day.
checklist.done: an HRIS fitness case exists naming the person, the office, the effective date and the two downstream owners.

checklist.step: Collect the signed fitness-and-propriety questionnaire and disclosure attestation
actions: Send the Officer Fitness Questionnaire through DocuSign covering the Form U4 Item 14 disclosure questions: criminal charges and convictions, regulatory actions, civil judicial actions, customer complaints, terminations, bankruptcies within 10 years, unsatisfied judgments and liens, and bonding denials.
Add the Rule 3110(e) authorisation to obtain employment, education and regulatory history and the 18 U.S.C. 1033 written-consent acknowledgement for insurance activity.
Chase any 'Yes' answer with a written explanation naming dates, forum, docket number and disposition before the file moves on.
File the executed envelope certificate and the completed questionnaire into the HRIS fitness case.
checklist.done: a signed questionnaire with a written explanation behind every 'Yes' answer is attached to the fitness case.

checklist.step: Search CRD and BrokerCheck for the nominee's full regulatory history
actions: Log in to FINRA Gateway and open CRD ▸ Individual Search; retrieve the nominee by CRD number, or by name and date of birth if unregistered.
Pull the Individual Snapshot, the Disclosure report and the full Form U4/U5 filing history from every prior firm.
Run the public BrokerCheck report separately and compare it line by line to the questionnaire answers; list every difference on the case.
Read every U5 the prior firms filed for a 'permitted to resign' or 'terminated for cause' reason and record the stated reason verbatim.
Export both reports to PDF named <surname>-CRD-<yyyy-mm-dd>.pdf and file them in the fitness case.
checklist.done: dated CRD and BrokerCheck extracts are on file and every difference against the questionnaire is written up.

checklist.step: Order the criminal, credit and sanctions background checks
actions: Order the officer-level package: 7-year county and federal criminal search in every county of residence, national criminal database, sex-offender registry, OFAC/SDN and global sanctions screen, and a credit report where the role has treasury or FinOp authority.
Confirm the FCRA pre-adverse-action disclosure and written authorisation were captured in the DocuSign packet before ordering.
Return any 'record found' result to Employment Counsel the same day with the underlying court record attached, not just the vendor summary.
Attach the completed vendor report and its completion date to the HRIS fitness case.
checklist.done: a completed criminal, sanctions and (where applicable) credit report is on file with any hit escalated to Employment Counsel.

checklist.step: Decide statutory disqualification and eligibility to serve
actions: Test every disclosure against Exchange Act Section 3(a)(39) and FINRA By-Laws Article III Section 3: felony or specified misdemeanour within 10 years, SRO or regulator bar or suspension, injunction, and false statements on a membership or registration application.
Where any limb is met, stop the appointment and open an MC-400 eligibility proceeding with FINRA before the person acts in a registered capacity.
Where no limb is met but adverse history exists, write a reasoned eligibility memo naming the facts, the rule tested and the heightened supervision conditions imposed.
Sign and date the memo and load it to the fitness case; an unsigned memo does not clear the appointment.
checklist.done: a dated counsel memo records the statutory-disqualification conclusion and any heightened supervision conditions.

checklist.step: Set the registration category and file the Form U4
actions: Map the office to the FINRA Rule 1220 category: Series 24 General Securities Principal, Series 26 Investment Company and Variable Contracts Principal, Series 27/28 Financial and Operations Principal, plus the SIE and Series 6 or 7 representative prerequisite.
In FINRA Gateway open Forms ▸ U4 and complete the registration request, disclosure pages and the Section 15 signature.
Where the person is already registered elsewhere, file the U4 amendment within 30 days of the firm learning of any new disclosable fact.
Enrol the person for any missing qualification exam through the CRD exam window and record the 120-day window expiry.
Save the filed U4 acknowledgement and CRD confirmation into the fitness case.
checklist.done: the U4 is filed with the correct principal category and the exam window, if any, is recorded with its expiry date.

checklist.step: Record the appointment decision in the board or committee minutes
actions: Add the appointment to the next board or Nominating and Governance Committee agenda in the board portal, with the counsel eligibility memo attached as a reading item.
Draft the resolution naming the person, the office, the effective date and any heightened supervision conditions counsel imposed.
Capture the vote and any recusal in the minutes and publish the approved minutes back to the portal.
Send the minute extract to the Head of Compliance so the fitness case can be closed.
checklist.done: a board or committee resolution naming the person, office and effective date is in the approved minutes.

checklist.step: Build the Firm Element covered-person roster for the year
actions: Extract from CRD the firm's full registered-person roster at January 1 with registration categories and branch assignment.
Join it to the producer management system to add product authority (variable annuity, variable life, mutual fund) and prior-year production.
Mark as covered persons all registered representatives with public customer contact, their immediate supervisors and the principals who approve their business, per Rule 1240(b)(1).
Reconcile the roster headcount to the HRIS active-registered headcount and resolve every difference before the needs analysis starts.
Publish the dated roster to the compliance evidence repository as the year's covered-person baseline.
checklist.done: a dated covered-person roster is published and reconciled to both CRD and HRIS headcount.

checklist.step: Run the annual Firm Element needs analysis
actions: Assemble the year's inputs: customer complaint themes, internal Rule 3120 testing findings, branch exam deficiencies, VA suitability exceptions under Rule 2330, advertising review rejections, FINRA exam findings and any Regulatory Notices issued during the year.
Add the product inputs from Product Development: new or repriced variable annuity riders, living-benefit changes and any share-class or fee change sold in the year.
Score each theme for risk and volume and record which covered-person population it applies to.
Write the needs-analysis document with the evidence reference behind every training topic and date it before the plan is drafted.
checklist.done: a dated needs-analysis document lists each training topic with the complaint, exam or product evidence that produced it.

checklist.step: Write the annual Firm Element training plan
actions: Convert each needs-analysis topic into a plan row: topic, learning objective, covered-person population, delivery method (e-learning, live branch session, webcast), duration, delivery window and owner.
Schedule every row to complete before December 31 and leave a December remediation window for late starters.

Cover the mandatory variable-product content: features, fees and surrender charges, living-benefit riders, exchange and replacement analysis under Rule 2330, and the Rule 2210(d)(1) and Rule 2211 communication standards.
Route the plan to the Head of Compliance for signature and store the signed plan in the compliance evidence repository.
checklist.done: a signed training plan maps every needs-analysis topic to a population, a delivery method and a completion date before December 31.

checklist.step: Build or refresh the courseware to the plan
actions: Create or version each course in the LMS course catalogue with the topic code from the training plan in the course title.
Embed the current product literature and the approved rider disclosure language supplied by Product Development, and cite the rule sections taught on the course reference slide.
Add a graded assessment with a stated pass mark (80% is the working standard) and unlimited retakes inside the delivery window.
Have the Marketing Compliance Analyst review any course slide that quotes product performance or rider values against Rule 2210(d)(1) before publication.
Publish the course version and record the version number against the plan row.
checklist.done: every plan row has a published, versioned course with a graded assessment and a compliance-reviewed content set.

checklist.step: Assign and deliver the courses to the covered-person roster
actions: Assign each course to its population using the dated covered-person roster, not a manager-maintained distribution list.
Set the LMS due date to the plan date and configure reminder mails at T-90, T-60 and T-30 days to December 31.
Run the live branch sessions and webcasts on the scheduled dates and load the attendance register into the LMS the same week.
Assign new joiners and newly registered persons within 10 business days of their registration approval date so mid-year hires are not missed.
checklist.done: every covered person carries an assignment for each course that applies to them, with a due date on or before December 31.

checklist.step: Track completion and chase non-completers weekly
actions: Run the LMS completion report every Monday from October 1 filtered to Status = Not Started or In Progress.
Send the branch manager and the supervising principal a named list of their outstanding people, not a percentage.
Escalate anyone still incomplete at T-30 to the Producer Compliance Manager and at T-10 to the Head of Compliance.
Record assessment scores and re-assign any person who fails the assessment after the permitted retakes.
checklist.done: a weekly named non-completer report is issued from October 1 and every escalation step is logged.

checklist.step: Restrict and remediate anyone incomplete at December 31
actions: On January 2 take the final completion extract and list every covered person incomplete at December 31.
Raise a GRC exception per person with the courses outstanding, the branch, the supervising principal and the root cause.
Impose the standing restriction: no new variable annuity business accepted from that person until completion, enforced by blocking their producer code in the new-business queue.
Set a remediation date inside 30 days and sign off personally when each person completes and the restriction lifts.
checklist.done: every December 31 non-completer has a logged exception, an enforced production restriction and a dated remediation plan.

checklist.step: Retain the cycle evidence for the full retention period
actions: Move the needs analysis, signed training plan, course version index, attendance registers, final completion extract and every officer fitness file into the repository under REG-014-C09 and the calendar year.
Apply the 6-year retention label with the first 3 years in the easily accessible tier per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4.
Confirm the repository index makes the record searchable by CRD number, course code and calendar year.
Record the retention expiry date on the index entry so nothing is destroyed early.
checklist.done: the cycle evidence is filed, labelled for 6-year retention and retrievable by CRD number and course code.

testing.step: Build the population of covered persons and appointments for the year
actions: Extract the firm's registered-person roster from CRD as at December 31 with registration category, branch and registration approval date.
Extract from Workday every officer, director and principal appointment or re-appointment with an effective date inside the calendar year.
Add mid-year joiners and leavers so persons registered in November cannot fall outside the population.
Sign the extract with the run date and record the row counts before any sampling.
testing.done: a dated, signed population of covered persons and in-year appointments exists with row counts recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the tested population to the roster compliance actually used
actions: Compare the audit population to the dated covered-person roster compliance published at the start of the cycle, person by person on CRD number.
List every person on the audit population who is absent from the compliance roster and establish why — late registration, branch transfer, or roster built from a stale extract.
Compare both to the HRIS active-registered headcount at December 31 as a third source.
Treat any unexplained omission from the compliance roster as an automatic exception; an untracked person cannot have been trained.
testing.done: every difference between the audit population, the compliance roster and HRIS headcount is explained or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of officer, director and principal appointments made in the year.
Take 40 covered persons selected at random from the roster using a recorded seed, stratified to include every branch and both new and long-tenured registrations.
Add 100% of persons who appeared on any weekly non-completer report after November 1.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date in the workpaper so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is drawn, reproducible from the recorded seed, and covers all in-year appointments and all late completers.

testing.step: Re-perform the needs analysis linkage to real-year evidence
actions: Pull the year's complaint log, Rule 3120 testing findings, branch exam deficiencies and Rule 2330 suitability exceptions independently of Compliance.
Take the five highest-volume themes from that evidence and check each appears as a topic in the needs analysis and the training plan.
Check every needs-analysis topic cites a specific evidence reference rather than a generic risk statement.
Treat a needs analysis that recycles the prior year's topics without new-year evidence as an exception.
testing.done: each of the top five in-year risk themes traces to a needs-analysis topic and a plan row, or is logged as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the fitness assessment for each sampled appointment
actions: In FINRA Gateway open CRD ▸ Individual Search and pull the Disclosure report for each sampled officer as it stood at the appointment date.
Reach your own view on disclosures and prior U5 reasons before opening the compliance fitness file.
Compare to the questionnaire answers and the counsel memo; an undisclosed CRD disclosure is an exception even where the conclusion was ultimately right.
Confirm the criminal, sanctions and credit reports pre-date the appointment effective date.
Screenshot the CRD disclosure page relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled appointment has an independent CRD re-performance note and a captured disclosure page.

testing.step: Test the statutory-disqualification conclusions
actions: Read each sampled counsel memo against Exchange Act 3(a)(39) and FINRA By-Laws Article III Section 3 as they read at the appointment date.
Confirm the memo tests each limb explicitly rather than concluding 'no disqualification' with no analysis.
Where heightened supervision was imposed, confirm the written supervisory conditions exist and the supervising principal acknowledged them in writing.
Where any limb was met, confirm an MC-400 was filed and FINRA approval obtained before the person acted.
testing.done: every sampled eligibility conclusion is supported by a limb-by-limb memo and, where required, an approved MC-400.

testing.step: Trace training completion to LMS records and to the delivered content
actions: For each sampled person open the LMS transcript and confirm every plan course applying to their population is assigned and marked Complete with a completion date on or before December 31.
Open the completed course version and confirm the content matches the plan topic — a legacy course re-used under a new topic code is an exception.
Confirm the assessment score meets the stated pass mark and that retakes were inside the delivery window.
For live sessions, trace the transcript entry back to the signed attendance register rather than accepting the LMS flag alone.
Export each sampled transcript into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled person's transcript shows complete, correctly versioned courses with pass-mark scores, evidenced in the workpaper.

testing.step: Recompute the deadline maths on completions and U4 amendments
actions: Recompute for each sampled person: completion date minus December 31 — any positive day count is a late completion.
For each sampled appointment recompute U4 filing date minus the date the firm learned of the disclosable fact and test it against the 30-day limit.
For newly registered persons recompute assignment date minus registration approval date and test it against the 10-business-day internal standard.
Recompute the firm-level completion rate at December 31 and compare it to the 100% threshold and the 2% escalation trigger.
testing.done: day counts are recomputed for completions and U4 filings and every breach of the 30-day or December 31 limit is quantified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the CRD number, the course or appointment, what was missed and the rule breached.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: roster built from a stale extract, assignment not made for a mid-year hire, course version mismatch, U4 filed late, screening ordered after the effective date.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and for any officer who acted before assessment close open a self-report assessment with Regulatory Counsel.
Carry every open exception into the following year's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception carries an issue reference, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compute the completion exception rate and the appointment exception count and compare them to the 100% and zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who authored no course and performed no sampled assessment, sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion and any open breaches to the Audit Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the exception rate and the Audit Committee reporting date, and is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the written supervisory procedures for registered-principal new-account approval and presents the annual policy set to the Board for approval; the Corporate Secretary owns the board record and the CEO owns the Rule 3130 certification

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA Rule 3110(b)(1) (written supervisory procedures), Rule 4512 (Customer Account Information), Rule 2330(b)/(c) (deferred variable annuity principal review), Rule 2330(e) (training) and Rule 3130 (annual CEO certification) re-read in the FINRA rulebook at each annual policy refresh

In-scope processes.value: New account opening for brokerage and variable annuity business — application intake, Rule 4512 account record capture, suitability capture, registered-principal review and approval, customer account record delivery — plus the annual board approval of the supervisory policy set and the Rule 3130 certification

In-scope systems.value: New-account workflow, principal approval queue and approval audit trail in the brokerage CRM; account records and disclosure delivery in the policy administration system; the approved policy set and minutes in the board portal

Compliance procedure documented.value: New Account Opening and Principal Approval WSP — account-type matrix, Rule 4512 required fields, suitability inputs, who may approve by registration category, evidence of approval, and the seven-business-day deferred variable annuity review standard

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Board on the recommendation of the Audit and Compliance Committee annually, and re-approved out of cycle on any FINRA rule change or after any principal-approval finding in an exam

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Deferred variable annuity applications reviewed and approved or rejected by a registered principal no later than seven business days after the office of supervisory jurisdiction receives a complete and correct application (Rule 2330(c)); Rule 4512 account record sent to the customer within 30 days of opening and at least every 36 months thereafter; Rule 3130 CEO certification executed annually before the board meeting at which it is presented

Deadline reminders configured.value: Brokerage CRM ages every unapproved deferred VA application and alerts the supervising principal at business day 3, the Producer Compliance Manager at day 5 and the Head of Compliance at day 6 of the seven-business-day clock; the 36-month account record refresh runs as a monthly due-list

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Approved account records, principal approval audit trail, suitability worksheets and customer record mailings retained 6 years after the account is closed per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4(e)(5); board minutes, approved policies and the Rule 3130 certification retained permanently in the board portal

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any account funded or any VA application submitted to the carrier without a recorded principal approval, and any approval recorded after the seventh business day, is logged as an exception with the account number, the principal, the root cause and the remediation date

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Records the board's approval of the policy set and the closure of any policy-level remediation the board directed, with the meeting date and resolution number

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every new brokerage and variable annuity account opened in the quarter across all branches and producer codes, taken from the brokerage CRM account-open log and reconciled to carrier-submitted applications; plus the year's board-approved policy versions

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any account funded without a documented principal approval, or any deferred VA approval later than seven business days after OSJ receipt, is a fail; more than one fail in a quarter suspends the branch's straight-through processing until re-tested

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Principal approval is a per-account control tested quarterly on a sample; the board policy approval is annual and tested once a year against the minutes and the signed policy versions

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must hold no supervisory principal role over any sampled branch and must not have approved any sampled account

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly new-account approval workpaper (population extract, carrier reconciliation, sample with seed, re-performance notes, day-count recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C10

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Account record set, principal approval audit trail and approval day-count report per sampled account, plus the board-approved WSP version history and Rule 3130 certification, producible for a FINRA cycle exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance responds to FINRA cycle exam requests and Rule 8210 letters; General Counsel clears any statement about missing principal approvals and the Corporate Secretary supplies certified minute extracts

checklist.step: Inventory the governance and supervisory policies that need board approval
actions: Open the board portal policy library and list every policy carrying a board-approval requirement, with its last approval date and resolution number.
Flag the broker-dealer set specifically: the Written Supervisory Procedures, the New Account Opening and Principal Approval WSP, the Rule 3120 supervisory control policy and the AML programme.
Mark any policy whose last approval is more than 12 months old as overdue and assign it a refresh owner.
Send the dated inventory to the Corporate Secretary for the annual governance calendar.
checklist.done: a dated policy inventory shows every board-approved policy with its approval date, owner and overdue flag.

checklist.step: Refresh the new-account WSP against the current rule text
actions: Open FINRA Rules 3110(b)(1), 4512, 2330 and 3130 in the FINRA online rulebook and note the last amendment date on each.
Redline the WSP where the rule text or a Regulatory Notice has moved, and record the notice number against each change.
Confirm the WSP names, for each account type, who may approve by registration category and what evidence of approval is required.
Circulate the redline to Regulatory Counsel and the branch supervising principals for comment with a fixed 10-business-day comment window.
checklist.done: a redlined WSP exists with every change tied to a rule amendment or Regulatory Notice and counsel comments resolved.

checklist.step: Define the Rule 4512 account record field set
actions: List the Rule 4512(a)(1) required fields: customer name and residence, whether of legal age, name of the associated person responsible for the account, signatures of the associated person and the approving principal, and for non-natural persons the names of persons authorised to transact.

Add the suitability inputs needed for variable annuity recommendations under Rule 2330(b): age, annual income, financial situation and needs, investment experience, investment objectives, time horizon, liquidity needs and risk tolerance.
Add the trusted contact person and the tax identification and citizenship fields.
Mark each field mandatory or conditional and hand the specification to the Business Systems Analyst for configuration.
checklist.done: a field specification names every Rule 4512 and Rule 2330(b) input with its mandatory or conditional status.

checklist.step: Configure the principal-approval gate in the brokerage workflow
actions: In Salesforce FSC open the New Account object and make every mandatory Rule 4512 field a validation rule so the record cannot be submitted incomplete.
Add an approval process that routes each submitted account to the queue of principals holding the required registration category, refreshed nightly from CRD.
Block account funding and carrier submission until the approval record is stamped, and record approver name, CRD number, timestamp and decision on the account.
Start a seven-business-day timer on deferred VA applications from the timestamp the OSJ marks the application complete and correct.
Test the gate in the sandbox with a deliberately incomplete application and confirm it is refused.
checklist.done: the workflow refuses incomplete accounts, routes to correctly registered principals and stamps an immutable approval record.

checklist.step: Capture the account record and suitability inputs at intake
actions: Key the completed application into the New Account record, entering every mandatory Rule 4512 field from the signed application, not from memory or the prior account.
Attach the signed application, the customer identification documents and, for a variable annuity, the signed disclosure and any replacement forms.
Mark the application 'complete and correct' only when no field is blank and no attachment is missing — this timestamp starts the seven-business-day clock.
Return incomplete applications to the producer the same day with a named list of missing fields rather than holding them in the queue.
checklist.done: the account record holds every mandatory field and attachment, and the complete-and-correct timestamp is set deliberately.

checklist.step: Perform the variable annuity suitability review before principal approval
actions: Open the suitability worksheet and test the Rule 2330(b) factors: the customer has been informed of surrender charges and periods, potential tax penalties, mortality and expense fees, investment advisory fees, and rider charges and limitations.

For any exchange, complete the replacement analysis: whether the customer has had another exchange within the preceding 36 months, the surrender charge on the contract being replaced, and the benefits lost.
Compare the recommended contract, share class and riders to the stated time horizon and liquidity needs and write a reasoned conclusion.
Attach the completed worksheet to the account record and mark the suitability status Pass, Fail or Refer.
checklist.done: a completed Rule 2330(b) worksheet with a reasoned conclusion and, for exchanges, a 36-month replacement analysis is on the record.

checklist.step: Have a registered principal review and approve each new account
actions: Open the principal approval queue and take accounts in complete-and-correct timestamp order, oldest first.
Read the application, the suitability worksheet and the attachments, and check the Rule 4512 fields against the signed application rather than the keyed record alone.
Approve, reject or return for more information, entering a written reason on any rejection or return.
For deferred variable annuities record the decision no later than the seventh business day after OSJ receipt, and note the business-day count on the approval.
Confirm the system stamped your name, CRD number and timestamp on the approval record before moving on.
checklist.done: each account carries a principal decision with a name, CRD number, timestamp and a written reason on every rejection.

checklist.step: Send the customer the account record within 30 days and refresh it every 36 months
actions: Run the daily approved-account extract and generate the Rule 4512 customer account record for each new account.
Despatch it to the customer's record address within 30 days of opening and log the despatch date and channel on the account.
Run the monthly 36-month due-list of existing accounts and send the record for verification with an update-or-confirm reply route.
Log every returned or undeliverable record and route it to the producer for an address investigation within 5 business days.
checklist.done: every account shows a despatch date within 30 days of opening and every 36-month due account has been re-sent or chased.

checklist.step: Work the unapproved and aged-application exception queue daily
actions: Run the aged report each morning: applications complete and correct for 3 or more business days without a principal decision, ordered by age.
Chase the named principal directly for anything at business day 5 and escalate to the Head of Compliance at business day 6.
Pull the separate report of accounts funded or submitted to the carrier without an approval record and treat each one as a breach, not a backlog item.
Record the daily queue position and the escalations in the supervisory log.
checklist.done: no application sits unapproved past business day 6 without an escalation recorded in the supervisory log.

checklist.step: Deliver the Rule 2330(e) training to producers and principals
actions: Assign the deferred variable annuity training to every registered representative who sells VAs and every principal who approves them.
Cover the material features of deferred variable annuities and the specific suitability and principal-review obligations under Rule 2330.
Set the completion deadline before the person may sell or approve their first VA and block their producer code until the transcript shows Complete.
Retain the attendance register and transcript extract for the annual Rule 2330(e) evidence pack.
checklist.done: no producer sells and no principal approves a deferred VA before the Rule 2330(e) transcript shows completion.

checklist.step: Produce the Rule 3120 annual supervisory control report
actions: Summarise the year's testing of the new-account approval control: population sizes, sample sizes, exception counts and day-count breaches.
State the changes made to the supervisory procedures during the year and the gaps that remain open with their remediation dates.
Submit the report to senior management by the annual due date and record the submission date.
Load the submitted report to the board portal as a reading item for the Audit and Compliance Committee.
checklist.done: the Rule 3120 report is submitted to senior management on time and lodged in the board portal.

checklist.step: Execute the Rule 3130 annual compliance certification
actions: Hold the documented annual meeting with the Chief Compliance Officer covering the compliance processes, the Rule 3120 findings and the open remediation items.
Read the Chief Compliance Officer's report evidencing the processes in place to establish, maintain, review, test and modify the compliance policies.
Sign the Rule 3130(b) certification naming the meeting date and the report relied on.
Give the signed certification to the Corporate Secretary for the board pack and the retained record set.
checklist.done: a signed Rule 3130 certification naming the meeting date and the underlying report is in the record set.

checklist.step: Take the policy set to the board for approval
actions: Load the refreshed WSP, the Rule 3120 report and the signed Rule 3130 certification into the board pack at least 5 business days before the meeting.
Draft the resolution approving each policy by name and version number and record the effective date of approval.
Capture the discussion, any board-directed changes, the vote and any recusal in the minutes.
Publish the approved minutes and issue a certified extract to the Head of Compliance.
checklist.done: the minutes record a resolution approving each named policy version with an effective date, and a certified extract is issued.

checklist.step: Publish the approved policy versions and retire the superseded ones
actions: Publish each board-approved policy at its new version number with the approval date and resolution number in the document header.
Move the superseded version to the archive with a retention label so the version in force on any past date can be evidenced.
Push a notification to all registered persons and branch principals naming the changed sections rather than attaching the whole document.
Confirm the branch WSP binders and the intranet link both resolve to the new version.
checklist.done: the current version is published everywhere, the superseded version is archived, and the change notice named the affected sections.

checklist.step: Retain the approval and governance record for the retention period
actions: Export the principal approval audit trail (approver, CRD number, timestamp, decision, day count) monthly into the repository under REG-014-C10.
Apply the 6-years-after-account-closure retention label to account records per SEA Rule 17a-4(e)(5) and the permanent label to minutes and certifications.
Confirm the record is searchable by account number, producer code, approving principal and approval date.
Record the retention expiry on the index entry so nothing is destroyed while an account remains open.
checklist.done: approval trails and governance records are filed, labelled to the correct retention period and searchable by account and principal.

testing.step: Build the population of accounts opened in the quarter
actions: Extract every new account record created in the quarter with branch, producer code, account type, complete-and-correct timestamp, approval timestamp and approver CRD number.
Add the deferred variable annuity applications separately, flagged new purchase versus exchange.
Include rejected and returned applications so a rejection cannot be used to hide an unapproved funded account.
Sign the extract with the run date and record the row count before sampling.
testing.done: a dated, signed population of all quarter accounts and VA applications exists with row counts recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the carrier and custodian source of record
actions: Extract every variable annuity contract issued in the quarter from the policy administration system and every brokerage account funded in the period.
Match to the CRM population on application number and contract number and list every issued contract with no CRM account record.
Investigate each unmatched contract with the branch — an application that reached the carrier outside the workflow is a control bypass, not a data gap.
Resolve or log every difference before sampling and record the reconciled counts in the workpaper.
testing.done: every issued contract and funded account reconciles to a CRM population row or is logged as a control bypass.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of deferred variable annuity exchanges and 100% of accounts for customers aged 65 or over.
Take 40 further accounts selected at random on a recorded seed, stratified across branches and approving principals so no principal is unsampled.
Add 100% of accounts that appeared on the aged-application report past business day 5.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers all exchanges, all senior-customer accounts and all aged applications.

testing.step: Re-perform the Rule 4512 account record check against the signed application
actions: Open the signed application image for each sampled account and read the Rule 4512(a)(1) fields off the paper: customer name and residence, legal age, responsible associated person, and the associated person and principal signatures.
Compare each field to the keyed CRM record and list every difference, including transposed dates of birth and stale addresses.
For non-natural persons confirm the names of those authorised to transact are recorded.
Treat a keyed field with no support on the signed application as an exception.
testing.done: every sampled account's keyed record agrees to the signed application or the difference is listed as an exception.

testing.step: Re-perform the principal approval judgement independently
actions: For each sampled account read the application and suitability worksheet and reach your own approve or reject conclusion before opening the principal's decision.
Compare to the recorded decision; a difference in conclusion, and an approval with no evidence the suitability worksheet was read, are both exceptions.
Confirm the approving principal held the required registration category on the approval date by checking CRD, not the internal role table.
Confirm the approval record carries name, CRD number, timestamp and decision and was not applied in bulk to a batch of accounts.
Capture the approval audit-trail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled approval has an independent re-performance conclusion and a captured audit-trail screen.

testing.step: Test the Rule 2330 suitability and replacement analysis on the VA sample
actions: Read each sampled worksheet and confirm every Rule 2330(b) factor is addressed with a customer-specific value, not a default.
For exchanges confirm the 36-month prior-exchange question was answered, the surrender charge on the replaced contract quantified and the benefits lost stated.
Test the recommended share class and riders against the stated time horizon and liquidity needs and challenge any long-surrender contract sold to a short horizon.
Treat a worksheet completed after the principal approval timestamp as a fail — the review must precede the approval.
testing.done: every sampled VA has a customer-specific worksheet completed before approval, with a quantified replacement analysis where applicable.

testing.step: Trace the customer account record delivery and the 36-month refresh
actions: For each sampled account pull the despatch log entry for the Rule 4512 customer account record and read the despatch date and channel.
Recompute despatch date minus account open date and test against the 30-day limit.
Take 10 accounts opened more than 36 months ago and confirm a refresh record was sent and the reply or non-reply logged.
Check undeliverable returns were routed to the producer and closed within 5 business days.
testing.done: every sampled account shows a delivery inside 30 days and the 36-month refresh sample is evidenced or logged as an exception.

testing.step: Recompute the seven-business-day approval clock
actions: For every sampled deferred VA recompute business days from the OSJ complete-and-correct timestamp to the principal approval timestamp, excluding weekends and market holidays.
Compare your count to the system-recorded day count and investigate any difference in the timer configuration.
Test whether the complete-and-correct flag was set only when the file was genuinely complete — a flag set late to reset the clock is a manipulation finding, not a timing exception.
List every approval beyond seven business days with the customer, branch, principal and day count.
testing.done: business-day counts are independently recomputed for every sampled VA and every breach beyond seven days is quantified and attributed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the account number, branch, approving principal, the rule breached and the customer impact.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: workflow bypassed, principal unregistered for the category, suitability worksheet completed after approval, complete-and-correct flag set late, account record not despatched.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and, where an account was funded without approval, require the account to be re-reviewed and the customer position assessed for rescission.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue reference, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Test the annual board approval and conclude with independent sign-off
actions: Open the board minutes for the year and confirm a resolution approves each supervisory policy by name and version number, with the effective date recorded.
Confirm the approved version number matches the version published in the document repository and in the branch binders on that date.
Confirm the signed Rule 3130 certification and the Rule 3120 report were before the board and are named in the minutes.

Compute the quarterly exception rate against the zero-tolerance threshold, write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — and have the independent reviewer who approved no sampled account sign and date the workpaper.
Report the conclusion to the Audit and Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion and exception rate, and evidences the board resolution approving each named policy version.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the Rule 3120 risk-based testing programme covering variable annuity sales practices, communications, AML and Reg BI, and owns the pre-market-entry authority gate that confirms the writing company holds a Certificate of Authority for the state and line before any business is solicited

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA Rule 3120 (Supervisory Control System) and Rule 3110 read in the FINRA rulebook at each annual plan refresh, together with Rule 3110(e), SEA Rule 17f-2, SEC Regulation Best Interest and the state Certificate of Authority statutes for each state added to the writing footprint

In-scope processes.value: Market-entry authority gate (state and line Certificate of Authority plus FINRA and state securities registration before first solicitation) and the annual risk-based testing cycle over VA sales practices, retail communications, AML and Reg BI, executed independent of the business line

In-scope systems.value: Risk assessment, test plan, workpapers and remediation tracking held in the testing platform; state authority evidence and filing correspondence in the regulatory filing portal and the internal regulatory system

Compliance procedure documented.value: Supervisory Control and Risk-Based Testing Procedure — annual risk assessment method, coverage rules for high-risk areas, independence requirement, sampling standard, exception rating scale and remediation tracking to closure; plus the Market Entry Authority Gate checklist

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and noted by the Audit and Compliance Committee before the plan year opens; re-approved on any change in writing footprint or after any FINRA finding on supervisory controls

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Authority gate must close before the first solicitation in a new state or line; a Rule 1017 continuing membership application for a material business expansion must be approved before the expansion is effected, and FINRA has 30 days to request further information after filing; the annual Rule 3120 report goes to senior management within the plan year

Deadline reminders configured.value: Testing platform milestone alerts at plan start, mid-year and 60 days before year end for any test not yet fieldwork-complete; market-entry gate alerts at T-90, T-60 and T-30 days to the announced first-writing date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Risk assessment, approved test plan, workpapers, sample lists, exception log and remediation closure evidence retained 6 years per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4; Certificates of Authority and state approval letters retained for the life of the authority plus 6 years

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Each test finding is logged with a severity rating, the rule breached, the business owner, the agreed action and the closure date; any business written in a state or line before the authority gate closed is logged as a regulatory breach and routed to Regulatory Counsel

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the closure of every high and medium finding after re-testing, and personally clears any market-entry gate exception

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The plan year's completed test files across VA sales practices, retail communications, AML and Reg BI, together with every state and line added to the writing footprint during the year and the business written in each from the announced first-writing date

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on business solicited in a state or line before the Certificate of Authority and registrations were in force; the testing programme fails if any designated high-risk area is unexecuted in the plan year or if more than 10% of high findings breach their agreed closure date

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The Rule 3120 programme is annual with quarterly fieldwork waves; the authority gate is per market entry and is tested every time a state or line is added, plus an annual footprint reconciliation

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Internal Audit reviews the testing programme itself; no reviewer may have performed, supervised or been the business owner of a sampled test

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual Rule 3120 programme quality workpaper (plan-to-execution reconciliation, sample of test files re-performed, footprint reconciliation, finding ageing) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C11

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Risk assessment, approved plan, executed workpapers with sample lists, the finding register with ageing, and the Certificate of Authority set by state and line, producible for a FINRA cycle exam or a state market conduct exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance owns the FINRA Rule 8210 and state market conduct responses; Regulatory Counsel clears any disclosure of unauthorised writing before it is sent and decides whether a voluntary state self-report is required

checklist.step: Confirm the writing entity's authority before any new state or line is opened
actions: Take the market-entry request from Distribution naming the state, the line of authority, the writing company and the announced first-writing date.

Open the company's licence register and confirm the Certificate of Authority for that state names the exact line — variable annuity and variable life sit under life with a separate variable authority in most states.
Confirm the state insurance department's active-company lookup shows the company in good standing and the annual continuation fee paid.
Where the line is not covered, open an expansion-of-authority application with the state before any solicitation and record the filing date and tracking number.
Record the conclusion, the evidence link and the earliest lawful solicitation date on the market-entry record.
checklist.done: the market-entry record shows the Certificate of Authority covers the state and line, with the earliest lawful solicitation date stated.

checklist.step: Confirm the securities-side registrations for the same footprint
actions: Confirm the broker-dealer is registered in the state through CRD Form BD state registration and that the state's blue-sky notice filing for the variable product is current.
Confirm every producer who will solicit holds both the state insurance licence with variable authority and an active Series 6 or 7 registration in that state.
Where the entry is a material expansion of business, test it against FINRA Rule 1017 and file a continuing membership application before the expansion is effected.
Write a short authority memo naming each registration relied on and its effective date, and sign it.
checklist.done: a signed authority memo names the insurance, broker-dealer and producer registrations relied on for the state and line.

checklist.step: Arm the systems gate so business cannot be written ahead of authority
actions: Load the state and line into the writing-company authority table with the earliest lawful solicitation date, not the announced launch date.
Configure the new-business rule to reject any application whose signed date precedes the earliest lawful solicitation date for that state and line.
Mirror the same block on the producer code so an unlicensed producer in that state cannot be attached to the application.
Test the block in the non-production environment with a back-dated application and confirm the rejection message names the authority reason.
checklist.done: the system rejects any application in the state or line dated before the earliest lawful solicitation date, proven by a test rejection.

checklist.step: Build the annual risk assessment behind the testing plan
actions: Score each business area on inherent risk using the year's data: VA sales volume and exchange rate, complaint volume by theme, advertising rejection rate, AML alert and SAR volume, and Reg BI disclosure exceptions.
Overlay control maturity from the prior year's findings and their closure record.
Rank the areas and mark VA sales practices, retail communications, AML and Reg BI as mandatory-coverage high-risk areas regardless of score.
Record the data source and run date behind every score so the assessment can be re-performed.
checklist.done: a dated risk assessment ranks every area with a cited data source and marks the four mandatory high-risk areas.

checklist.step: Write and approve the risk-based testing plan
actions: Convert each in-scope area into a test row: objective, rule tested, population definition, sample method and size, tester, quarter of fieldwork and reporting date.
Assign every test to a tester outside the business line being tested and record the independence confirmation on the row.
Set the sampling standard: minimum 25 items per test, 100% coverage of senior-customer VA exchanges and of any area with an open prior-year high finding.
Sign the plan, present it to the Audit and Compliance Committee and lock the baseline version so plan changes are visible.
checklist.done: a signed, baselined plan covers all four mandatory areas with an independent tester and a fieldwork quarter on every row.

checklist.step: Test variable annuity sales practices
actions: Pull the population of VA transactions for the quarter split into new purchases, exchanges and additional deposits.
Sample 100% of exchanges and senior-customer sales plus 25 random new purchases on a recorded seed.

Test each file for the Rule 2330(b) suitability factors, the 36-month prior-exchange question, the surrender-charge quantification on the replaced contract and the principal approval inside seven business days.
Test rider recommendations against the stated time horizon and liquidity needs and challenge any long-surrender contract sold to a customer with a short horizon.
Write each deviation into the workpaper with the account number, the producer and the rule breached.
checklist.done: the VA sales-practice test file holds a sampled, re-performed suitability conclusion for every selected transaction.

checklist.step: Test retail communications and variable product advertising
actions: Extract every retail communication distributed in the quarter from the marketing platform and the branch-produced material log, including seminar decks and social posts.
Sample 30 items weighted to variable annuity and variable life material.

Test each against Rule 2210(d)(1): fair and balanced, no false or exaggerated claims, no prediction of future performance, and required risk and fee disclosure; and against Rule 2211 for variable product specifics including the guarantee source and the separate account explanation.
Confirm a registered principal approved each item before first use under Rule 2210(b)(1) and that filed items reached FINRA Advertising Regulation within 10 business days of first use.
Log any item distributed without approval as a finding naming the originator and the distribution channel.
checklist.done: the communications test file records a rule-by-rule conclusion and the approval and filing evidence for every sampled item.

checklist.step: Test the AML programme over variable product business
actions: Pull the quarter's alert population from the AML platform with alert type, disposition and closure date, plus every SAR filed and every 314(a) response.
Sample 25 closed alerts weighted to early-surrender and large single-premium VA activity.
Re-perform the disposition: read the customer profile, the source of funds narrative and the transaction pattern and reach your own escalate or close conclusion.
Test the customer identification programme evidence and the beneficial ownership record for each sampled new account.
Recompute the SAR filing clock at 30 calendar days from initial detection and list any late filing.
checklist.done: the AML test file records an independent disposition conclusion per sampled alert and a recomputed SAR filing day count.

checklist.step: Test Regulation Best Interest compliance
actions: Sample 25 recommendations to retail customers across VA, mutual fund and rollover recommendations.
Test the Disclosure Obligation: Form CRS delivered at or before the recommendation, and the material fees, conflicts and limitations disclosed in writing.
Test the Care Obligation: reasonable-basis, customer-specific and series-of-recommendations analysis documented, including a cost comparison of reasonably available alternatives.
Test the Conflict of Interest Obligation: the producer's compensation differential on the recommended product identified and mitigated.
Record for each file whether the documented rationale would stand up without the producer's later explanation.
checklist.done: each sampled recommendation has a documented conclusion on the Disclosure, Care and Conflict obligations with the evidence cited.

checklist.step: Rate each finding and agree the remediation with the business owner
actions: Raise a GRC finding per deviation naming the area, the rule breached, the sample items affected and the extrapolated population impact.
Rate severity: high where customer harm or a reportable breach exists, medium where the control failed without customer impact, low where the evidence was incomplete.
Agree the corrective action, the named business owner and a closure date — 60 days for high, 90 for medium, 180 for low from the report date.
Refuse an action described only as 'reinforce with the team'; require a system, procedure or supervisory change.
checklist.done: every finding has a severity rating, a named business owner, a concrete corrective action and a dated closure commitment.

checklist.step: Track remediation to closure and re-test before closing
actions: Run the finding ageing report monthly and escalate anything within 15 days of its closure date and not yet evidenced.
For each proposed closure, obtain the evidence — the amended procedure, the system release note, the re-trained population extract — and attach it to the finding.
Re-test a sample of 10 items post-remediation for every high finding before it may be closed.
Escalate any date extension request to the Head of Compliance with the reason and the new date, and never extend twice silently.
checklist.done: no high finding closes without post-remediation re-test evidence, and every extension is approved and recorded.

checklist.step: Reconcile the annual writing footprint against held authority
actions: Extract every state and line in which business was written during the year from the policy administration system.
Match each state and line to a Certificate of Authority effective before the earliest policy issue date in that state.
List any state or line written without matching authority and route it to Regulatory Counsel the same day for a self-report assessment.
Confirm every held Certificate of Authority is still current and the annual continuation fee is paid, and file the state confirmations.
checklist.done: every written state and line matches a Certificate of Authority in force before the first policy, or is escalated to counsel.

checklist.step: Report the programme results to senior management under Rule 3120
actions: Summarise the plan-versus-executed position by area with sample sizes, exception counts and severity mix.
State the supervisory procedure changes made during the year and the findings still open with their revised dates.
Submit the report to senior management inside the plan year and record the submission date and recipients.
Table the report at the Audit and Compliance Committee and record the committee's directions in the finding register.
checklist.done: the Rule 3120 report is submitted inside the plan year and the committee's directions are recorded against findings.

checklist.step: Escalate an unexecuted high-risk test or a blocked remediation
actions: Review the plan-versus-executed position at each quarter end and identify any mandatory high-risk test not yet in fieldwork.
Where a test cannot be executed in the plan year, require a written decision naming the reason, the interim compensating control and the revised date.
Where a business owner will not fund or accept a remediation, escalate to the Audit and Compliance Committee with the residual risk quantified.
Record the decision and its owner in the finding register — deferring a mandatory area without a compensating control is not an available outcome.
checklist.done: every unexecuted mandatory test or blocked remediation has a written, owned decision and a compensating control.

checklist.step: Retain the programme evidence for the retention period
actions: Move the risk assessment, signed plan, executed workpapers, sample lists, finding register and closure evidence into the repository under REG-014-C11 and the plan year.
File the Certificate of Authority set by state and line alongside, with the effective and continuation dates on the index entry.
Apply the 6-year retention label with the first 3 years in the easily accessible tier per SEA Rule 17a-4.
Confirm the record is searchable by area, rule cited, finding severity and state.
checklist.done: the programme evidence and authority set are filed, labelled for 6-year retention and searchable by area, rule and state.

testing.step: Build the population of planned tests and written states for the year
actions: Extract the baselined test plan with every row's area, tester, fieldwork quarter and status at year end.
Extract every state and line in which policies were issued in the year from the policy administration system with the earliest issue date per state.
Add every plan change made after baseline, with the date and the approver, so silent scope reduction is visible.
Sign the extract with the run date and record the counts before sampling.
testing.done: a dated, signed population of planned tests, plan changes and written states exists with counts recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile executed tests to the plan and to the risk assessment
actions: Match each baselined plan row to a completed workpaper and list every row with no workpaper or a status of deferred.
Confirm all four mandatory high-risk areas — VA sales practices, communications, AML, Reg BI — were executed in the plan year.
Trace the plan rows back to the risk assessment and list any area ranked high in the assessment but absent from the plan.
Treat any post-baseline scope reduction without a recorded approver as an automatic exception.
testing.done: every planned test reconciles to a workpaper or an approved deferral, and all four mandatory areas are evidenced as executed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of test files and states
actions: Take 100% of the four mandatory high-risk area test files and 100% of states or lines added to the footprint during the year.
Take 8 further test files at random from the remaining plan rows on a recorded seed.
Add 100% of findings rated high and 15 findings rated medium selected at random.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers all mandatory areas, all new states and all high findings.

testing.step: Verify tester independence from the business line tested
actions: For each sampled test file read the tester name and trace their reporting line in Workday at the fieldwork date.
Confirm the tester did not report into, and was not compensated on the results of, the business area tested.
Confirm no tester tested a control they designed or operated in the prior 12 months.
Treat a test performed by the control owner as an invalid test, not an independence observation.
testing.done: every sampled test file is evidenced as performed by a tester independent of the area tested, or is invalidated.

testing.step: Re-perform the key judgement in each sampled test file
actions: Re-select 5 items from each sampled test's own population using the tester's recorded sampling method and confirm the method reproduces their sample.
Re-perform the tester's conclusion on 5 items per file — the suitability call, the Rule 2210(d)(1) content call, the AML disposition or the Reg BI care analysis as applicable.
Compare to the tester's recorded conclusion; a difference in conclusion, or a conclusion with no evidence attached, is an exception.
Capture the source screen or document relied on for each re-performance into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled test file has an independent re-performance on 5 items with the source evidence captured.

testing.step: Re-perform the market-entry authority gate for every new state
actions: For each state added in the year open the state insurance department's company lookup and read the Certificate of Authority lines and effective date directly.
Confirm the variable authority — not merely the life authority — was in force before the earliest policy issue date in that state.
Confirm the broker-dealer's state registration and the blue-sky notice filing for the product were effective on the same date.
Where any registration post-dates the first policy, quantify the affected policies and open a self-report assessment.
testing.done: each new state's authority is independently verified as effective before the first policy, or the affected policies are quantified.

testing.step: Trace sampled findings to evidence and to identifiable population items
actions: For each sampled finding open the GRC record and confirm it names the affected account numbers, producer codes or communication identifiers rather than a generic description.
Trace the finding back to the workpaper item that produced it and forward to the closure evidence attached.
Confirm high findings carry post-remediation re-test evidence on at least 10 items before closure.
Treat a finding closed on an assertion of completion with no attached artefact as still open.
testing.done: every sampled finding traces to identified population items and, where closed, to attached remediation and re-test evidence.

testing.step: Recompute finding ageing and the closure-breach rate
actions: Recompute each finding's days open from report date to closure date, or to the test date if still open.
Test each against its severity limit: 60 days for high, 90 for medium, 180 for low, counting from the report date not the latest extension.
Compute the proportion of high findings that breached their original closure date and compare it to the 10% threshold.
List every finding extended more than once and check each extension carries an approval by the Head of Compliance.
testing.done: finding ageing is independently recomputed, the high-finding breach rate is computed against the 10% threshold and repeat extensions are listed.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the test file or state, what failed and the rule or programme standard breached.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: mandatory area unexecuted, tester not independent, sample below the minimum, conclusion unsupported, finding closed without evidence, business written before authority.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and route any writing-before-authority exception to Regulatory Counsel for a state self-report decision within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the following year's programme review as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue reference, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare executed mandatory coverage to the required four areas and the high-finding breach rate to the 10% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the workpaper references and any unauthorised writing identified.
Have the independent reviewer, who performed no sampled test and owns no sampled finding, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit and Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the coverage position and the breach rate, and is filed with a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns continuous FINRA membership for the broker-dealer that distributes variable insurance products, the Rule 1017 continuing membership application for any material change in ownership, control or business, and the membership agreement restriction register

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA By-Laws Article III (qualifications of members and associated persons) and FINRA Rule 1017 (Application for Approval of Change in Ownership, Control, or Business Operations) read against the current membership agreement, together with Rule 2210(b)(1) principal approval and Rule 2210(c)(1) filing of retail communications

In-scope processes.value: Broker-dealer membership maintenance (membership agreement restrictions, Form BD amendments, annual assessments) and the change-control gate that catches any material change in ownership, control, business lines, personnel or facilities before it is effected — including new variable product lines, new distribution channels and material personnel changes

In-scope systems.value: Membership agreement, restriction register, Form BD versions and CMA correspondence held in the regulatory system; Form BD and CMA filed through FINRA Gateway; retail communications approved and filed from the marketing platform

Compliance procedure documented.value: Membership Maintenance and Material Change Procedure — the restriction register, the change-materiality test against the Rule 1017(a) triggers, the pre-effect filing gate, the safe harbour test under IM-1011-1, and the Form BD amendment routine

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with General Counsel concurrence; re-approved annually and whenever FINRA amends the membership rules or the firm's membership agreement is varied

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Rule 1017 CMA filed and approved before the material change is effected; Form BD amendments filed promptly and in any event within 30 days of the change; annual FINRA assessment and Annual Audited Report filed on the schedule set by SEA Rule 17a-5; retail communications filed with FINRA Advertising Regulation within 10 business days of first use, or 10 business days before first use during the first year of membership

Deadline reminders configured.value: Change-control board calendar alerts at T-120, T-90 and T-60 days to any announced material change effective date so the CMA can be filed with time for FINRA's 30-day information request; Form BD amendment alerts at day 10, 20 and 25 of the 30-day clock

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Membership agreement, restriction register, all CMA filings and FINRA decision letters, Form BD versions and change-control minutes retained for the life of the membership plus 6 years per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4(b)

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any material change effected before FINRA approval, any activity outside a membership agreement restriction, and any Form BD amendment filed after 30 days is logged as a regulatory exception with the change reference, the root cause and a Regulatory Counsel disposition

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Clears every materiality determination that concludes no CMA is required and signs off the remediation of any change effected without approval

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every change-control record, board or executive committee decision, new product launch, channel launch, executive appointment and ownership movement in the period, tested against the Rule 1017(a) triggers and against the membership agreement restrictions

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance — any material change effected before FINRA approval, or any business conducted outside a membership agreement restriction, is a fail regardless of intent; a single fail escalates to the Board and triggers a Regulatory Counsel self-report assessment

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: Membership is a continuous obligation; the test runs semi-annually over the period's change population, with an immediate targeted test on any acquisition, new product line or change of control

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not have prepared any sampled materiality determination or CMA filing

Evidence location for test results.value: Semi-annual membership maintenance workpaper (change population, materiality re-performance, CMA and Form BD tracing, restriction reconciliation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C12

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Current membership agreement with the restriction register, the CMA filing set with FINRA decision letters, the Form BD version history and the change-control minutes, producible on a FINRA membership examination request within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Regulatory Affairs Manager is the named contact for the FINRA Membership Application Program; General Counsel clears any response conceding an unapproved change, and the Head of Compliance handles Rule 8210 requests

checklist.step: Maintain the membership agreement and its restriction register
actions: Load the current FINRA membership agreement into the regulatory system and extract each restriction into its own register row: permitted business lines, number of registered persons, number of branch offices, permitted product types, and any capital or supervisory condition.
Record against each restriction the current actual position — headcount, branch count, product set — refreshed monthly from HRIS and CRD.
Set a threshold alert at 80% of any numeric restriction so an approach to the limit is visible before it is breached.
Publish the register to the change-control board and the Head of Compliance each month.
checklist.done: the restriction register lists every membership agreement condition with the current actual position and an 80% threshold alert.

checklist.step: Route every business change through a materiality gate
actions: Require every new product, new distribution channel, new office, ownership movement, executive appointment and outsourcing arrangement to be raised as a change record before commitment.
