Test each against the Rule 1017(a) triggers: merger with another member, direct or indirect acquisition of another member, direct or indirect acquisition or transfer of 25% or more of the member's assets or any asset or line of business generating 25% or more of earnings or revenue, change in equity ownership or partnership capital that results in one person or entity owning 25% or more, and a material change in business operations.

Test material change in business operations against IM-1011-1 examples: removing or modifying a membership agreement restriction, market making, underwriting or proprietary trading for the first time, and adding business activities requiring a higher net capital.
Record the tested trigger, the answer and the evidence on the change record; never record a bare 'not material'.
checklist.done: every change record shows each Rule 1017(a) trigger tested with an evidenced answer and a materiality conclusion.

checklist.step: Have counsel clear every 'no CMA required' determination
actions: Read each not-material determination against the rule text and IM-1011-1 as they read at the determination date.

Apply the IM-1011-1 safe harbour arithmetic where relied on: the permitted percentage increases in associated persons, offices and markets over a rolling 12 months, and confirm the firm is not excluded from the safe harbour by a disciplinary history or a restriction.
Confirm or overturn the determination in writing on the change record, with your name and the date.
Send overturned determinations back to the Regulatory Affairs Manager the same week to open a CMA.
checklist.done: no material-change determination closes without a dated counsel confirmation and, where relied on, the safe harbour arithmetic shown.

checklist.step: Prepare the continuing membership application
actions: Open the CMA in the FINRA Gateway Membership Application Program and select the Rule 1017 change type.

Assemble the standards-of-admission narrative against the Rule 1014 standards: supervisory system, written supervisory procedures, personnel qualifications, facilities, communications and operational systems, and financial controls.

Attach the business plan, three-year pro forma financials, the net capital computation under the proposed business, the organisation chart with registration categories and the revised written supervisory procedures.
Have the Chief Financial Officer confirm the net capital computation in writing and attach the confirmation.
Pay the application fee and record the filing date and MAP reference on the change record.
checklist.done: the CMA is filed with the Rule 1014 narrative, pro formas, net capital computation and revised WSPs, and the MAP reference is recorded.

checklist.step: Hold the change until FINRA approves it
actions: Set the change record status to 'Blocked — CMA pending' and record the block in the project plan so implementation cannot proceed on schedule pressure.
Instruct Distribution, Product and IT in writing that no solicitation, contracting, system configuration or hiring against the change may go live before the decision letter.
Track FINRA's 30-day window for a request for further information and answer any request inside the stated response period.
Escalate to the Chief Executive Officer where the business proposes to proceed ahead of approval — proceeding is not an available option.
checklist.done: the change is formally blocked, the block is communicated in writing and FINRA information requests are answered inside the stated period.

checklist.step: Record the FINRA decision and update the membership agreement
actions: File the FINRA decision letter against the change record and read every condition or restriction imposed.
Amend the restriction register with the new or varied restrictions and their effective dates.
Release the implementation block only after the effective date in the decision letter, and record who released it and when.
Circulate the changed restrictions to the Head of Compliance, Distribution and the branch principals with the sections that changed named.
checklist.done: the decision letter is filed, the restriction register reflects every imposed condition, and the block release is dated and attributed.

checklist.step: Keep Form BD current
actions: Monitor the triggers for a Form BD amendment: change of address or branch offices, direct owners and executive officers, indirect owners, control affiliates, types of business, and disclosure events.

In FINRA Gateway open Forms ▸ BD Amendment, update the affected schedules — Schedule A and B for direct and indirect owners, Schedule C for changes, Schedule D for other business — and file within 30 days of the change.
Confirm the filed version returns from CRD without a deficiency notice and file the acknowledgement.
Reconcile the filed Form BD to the corporate register held by the Corporate Secretary each quarter.
checklist.done: Form BD reflects the current ownership, officers, branches and business types, filed within 30 days and reconciled to the corporate register.

checklist.step: Keep the firm's registrations and assessments current
actions: Track the FINRA annual assessment invoice and the Annual Audited Report deadline under SEA Rule 17a-5 and hand each to Finance with the due date.
Confirm the SIPC assessment and the state broker-dealer registrations are renewed on the FINRA Renewal Program cycle.
Check the firm's CRD record each quarter for lapsed state registrations and open any renewal that failed to process.
Log each payment and filing with its date and confirmation number in the regulatory system.
checklist.done: every membership assessment, annual report and state registration is current with a logged payment or filing confirmation.

checklist.step: Have a registered principal approve every retail communication before first use
actions: Route each retail communication to a registered principal for Rule 2210(b)(1) approval before first use and capture the approver name, CRD number, date and the version approved.

Test the content against Rule 2210(d)(1) and, for variable products, Rule 2211 — the insurance company guarantee, separate account explanation, surrender charges, fees and no implication of a guaranteed return.
Refuse to release any version that was edited after approval; a changed version needs a fresh approval.
Store the approved artwork and the approval record against the campaign in the marketing platform.
checklist.done: every retail communication carries a pre-use principal approval naming the approver, date and approved version.

checklist.step: File the communications that require FINRA filing within the deadline
actions: Identify filing-required categories: retail communications concerning registered investment companies and variable insurance products, and all retail communications during the first year of membership.

File through the FINRA Advertising Regulation Electronic Filing system within 10 business days of first use — or 10 business days before first use for a new member, and before first use for the categories requiring pre-use filing.
Record the filing reference, the filing date and the first-use date on the campaign record and recompute the day count on filing.
Work every Advertising Regulation comment letter to closure and withdraw or amend the piece where required, recording the corrective action.
checklist.done: every filing-required communication has a filing reference with a recomputed day count inside the 10-business-day limit.

checklist.step: Reconcile actual business activity to the membership agreement monthly
actions: Extract the month's transaction and product mix from the policy administration and brokerage systems and map each product type to a permitted business line on the membership agreement.
Compare registered headcount and branch count to the agreement limits and flag anything above 80% of a limit.
Investigate any transaction in a product type not listed as permitted and stop the activity the same day pending a materiality determination.
Sign and file the monthly reconciliation whether or not exceptions arose.
checklist.done: a signed monthly reconciliation shows every traded product type mapped to a permitted line and headcount and branches within limits.

checklist.step: Prepare the annual membership and change-control report for the board
actions: Summarise the year: changes raised, materiality determinations made, CMAs filed and their outcomes, restrictions varied, and any activity stopped for falling outside the agreement.
State the current position against every numeric restriction and the projected position given the business plan.
Load the report to the board portal with the current membership agreement attached.
Record the board's directions on any restriction approaching its limit.
checklist.done: the board has a report stating CMA outcomes, restriction headroom and any activity stopped, with directions recorded.

checklist.step: Escalate any change effected without approval
actions: On discovery, stop the activity the same day and quantify what was done — transactions, customers, revenue and dates.
Assess the self-report position under FINRA Rule 4530 and decide whether the firm reports to the Membership Application Program, to Enforcement, or both.
Prepare the remedial CMA or membership agreement variation and file it with a full chronology.
Record the decision, the filing and the customer remediation, if any, on the change record and inform the Board.
checklist.done: unapproved activity is stopped and quantified the same day, with a documented self-report decision and a remedial filing.

checklist.step: Refresh the membership evidence pack for examination readiness
actions: Assemble each quarter: the current membership agreement, the restriction register with actuals, the CMA set with decision letters, the Form BD version history and the change-control minutes.
Confirm every document is the current version and that superseded versions are archived with their in-force dates.
Test retrieval by asking a colleague to produce the current agreement and the last CMA decision letter inside 30 minutes.
Record the pack refresh date on the repository index.
checklist.done: a current, retrievable membership evidence pack exists with a recorded quarterly refresh date.

checklist.step: Retain the membership record for the required period
actions: File the membership agreement, every CMA and decision letter, Form BD versions and change-control determinations under REG-014-C12 with their effective dates.
Apply the life-of-membership plus 6 years retention label per SEA Rule 17a-4(b) so nothing is destroyed while the membership subsists.
Confirm the record is searchable by change reference, MAP reference, Form BD filing date and restriction.
Record the retention expiry on the index entry.
checklist.done: the membership record set is filed, labelled for life-of-membership plus 6 years and searchable by change and MAP reference.

testing.step: Build the population of business changes in the period
actions: Extract every change-control record raised in the period with its materiality conclusion, counsel clearance and effective date.
Independently extract board and executive committee minutes, new product approvals, new branch openings, executive appointments from Workday and share-register movements from the Corporate Secretary.
Add the month-end product mix extracts so a new product type traded without a change record is visible.
Sign the extract with the run date and record the counts before sampling.
testing.done: a dated, signed population of changes drawn from change control, minutes, HR and traded product mix exists with counts recorded.

testing.step: Reconcile the change population to independent evidence of what actually changed
actions: Match each board-approved initiative, new product type traded, new branch and executive appointment to a change-control record.
List every real-world change with no change record — a change that never entered the gate could never have been tested for materiality.
Compare the share register movements to the Form BD Schedule A and B ownership as filed.
Resolve or log every difference before sampling.
testing.done: every independently evidenced change matches a change record or is logged as a gate bypass.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of changes concluded material and 100% of ownership, control and new-product-line changes regardless of conclusion.
Take 25 changes concluded not material, selected at random on a recorded seed across the period's months.
Add 100% of gate bypasses identified in the reconciliation.
Record the seed, population size and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers all material changes, all ownership changes and all gate bypasses.

testing.step: Re-perform the Rule 1017(a) materiality test on each sampled change
actions: Read the underlying business papers for each sampled change and reach your own conclusion on each Rule 1017(a) trigger before opening the recorded determination.
Recompute the 25% tests using the audited financials: asset transfer against total assets, and the line of business against earnings and revenue for the relevant period.
Recompute the equity ownership percentages after the movement, including indirect holdings through affiliates.
Compare to the recorded conclusion; a right answer supported by the wrong arithmetic is still an exception.
Capture the financial extract relied on into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled change has an independent materiality conclusion with the 25% arithmetic recomputed and the source extract captured.

testing.step: Test the safe harbour arithmetic where it was relied on
actions: Identify sampled determinations that relied on the IM-1011-1 safe harbour and read the recorded percentage increase in associated persons, offices or markets over the rolling 12 months.
Recompute the base figures from the CRD roster and the branch register at the start of the rolling period.
Confirm the firm was eligible for the safe harbour on the determination date — no disqualifying disciplinary history and no membership agreement restriction excluding it.
Treat reliance on the safe harbour by an ineligible firm as a fail, not a documentation gap.
testing.done: every safe harbour reliance is recomputed from CRD and branch source data and the firm's eligibility on the date is confirmed.

testing.step: Trace each material change to a filed CMA and a FINRA decision that pre-dates the effect
actions: In FINRA Gateway open the Membership Application Program record for each sampled material change and read the MAP reference, filing date and decision date.
Compare the decision date to the change's actual effective date taken from the system, contract or hiring record — not from the project plan.
Read the decision letter conditions and check each one is present in the restriction register.
Any effect before the decision date is a reportable regulatory breach, not a test exception.
Capture the MAP record and the decision letter into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled material change traces to a CMA decision dated before the actual effective date, with the conditions in the register.

testing.step: Trace Form BD amendments and communication filings to their deadlines
actions: For each sampled ownership, officer or branch change, open the Form BD filing history in CRD and read the filing date and the schedules amended.
Recompute filing date minus change date and test against the 30-day limit.

Sample 15 filing-required retail communications, read the first-use date from the campaign record and the filing date from the Advertising Regulation acknowledgement, and recompute the business-day count against the 10-business-day limit.
Confirm each sampled communication carries a principal approval dated before first use.
testing.done: Form BD and communication filing day counts are independently recomputed and every breach of the 30-day or 10-business-day limit is listed.

testing.step: Reconcile actual business activity to the membership agreement restrictions
actions: Extract the period's traded product types, registered headcount from CRD and branch count from the branch register.
Map every traded product type to a permitted business line in the membership agreement and list anything unmapped.
Compare headcount and branch count to the numeric restrictions at each month end, not just at period end.
Treat any month above a restriction as a breach even if the position was corrected before period end.
testing.done: every traded product type maps to a permitted line and every month-end headcount and branch count is tested against the limits.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the change reference, what was effected, when, and the rule or restriction breached.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: change never entered the gate, trigger untested, 25% arithmetic wrong, safe harbour misapplied, effected before decision, Form BD late, communication filed late.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and route every effected-before-approval exception to Regulatory Counsel for a Rule 4530 self-report decision within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the next semi-annual test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue reference, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the count of changes effected before approval and of activity outside the restrictions to the zero-tolerance threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the workpaper references and any self-report opened.
Have the independent reviewer, who prepared no sampled determination or CMA, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Board and the Audit and Compliance Committee at the next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the count of unapproved changes and the reporting date, and is filed in the repository.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the appointment and termination event pipeline — Form U4 and U5 filing inside 30 days, state appointment and termination notices inside each state's window, and the immediate refresh of the Firm Element covered-person roster when a producer joins, moves or leaves

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA By-Laws Article V Sections 2 and 3 (U4 and U5 filing within 30 days), FINRA Rule 1240(b) for the covered-person roster refresh, and each state's appointment and termination statute for the insurance side, re-read whenever a state changes its window

In-scope processes.value: Producer onboarding after contracting, intra-firm branch and supervisor transfers, voluntary and for-cause terminations, and the resulting appointment, termination, U4, U5 and training-roster events across every appointed state

In-scope systems.value: State appointments and terminations transacted through the NIPR Gateway; U4 and U5 filed in FINRA Gateway; the producer record of truth held in the producer management system and fed from HRIS

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Appointment and Termination Procedure — event triggers and SLAs, the appointment-before-solicitation rule, the U4/U5 30-day clock, for-cause termination language review, commission stop and roster refresh

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance and reviewed by Employment Counsel for the U5 termination-language standard; re-approved annually and on any state appointment-window change published in a bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Form U5 filed within 30 days of termination and any amended U5 within 30 days of learning new facts; Form U4 amendment within 30 days of learning of a disclosable event; state appointment filed within each state's window from the agency contract or first application date (commonly 15 days) and termination notice within the state window (commonly 30 days)

Deadline reminders configured.value: Producer management system SLA clocks per event with alerts at day 10, day 20 and day 25 of every 30-day clock and at day 5 and day 10 of the 15-day appointment window, escalating to the Producer Compliance Manager at the penultimate alert

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Appointment and termination confirmations from NIPR, filed U4 and U5 copies with CRD acknowledgements, the U5 copy sent to the producer and the roster refresh extracts retained 6 years per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4, and per state record rules where longer

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any solicitation before appointment, any U4 or U5 filed beyond 30 days and any termination without a state notice is logged with the producer number, the state, the day count and a dated remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every late U4 or U5 filing remediation and every case of business written before appointment, including the decision on customer and carrier notification

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every appointment, termination and transfer event in the quarter taken from the producer management system, reconciled to HRIS joiners and leavers, to NIPR appointment and termination confirmations and to the CRD registration history

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on business solicited or submitted before appointment in the state; any U4 or U5 filed beyond 30 days is a fail; a late-filing rate above 2% of the quarter's events suspends the licensing team's straight-through processing pending re-test

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is event-driven and continuous; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's event population, with 100% coverage of for-cause terminations regardless of quarter volume

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in Licensing Operations and must not have filed any sampled U4, U5 or appointment transaction

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly appointment and termination workpaper (event population, NIPR and CRD reconciliation, sample with seed, day-count recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C13

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-producer event file — contract date, appointment confirmation, first application date, U4 and U5 filing acknowledgements, termination notice and covered-person roster entry — producible for a state market conduct exam or a FINRA cycle exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers state department appointment and termination inquiries; Regulatory Counsel clears any U5 language dispute or admission of pre-appointment solicitation before it is sent

checklist.step: Open an appointment event the day the producer contract is signed
actions: Take the executed producer agreement from Distribution Operations with the signature date, the writing states requested and the product authorities requested.
Create the producer record with national producer number, tax identification number, business address and the requesting agency hierarchy.
Open one appointment event per state requested, and start the state's statutory clock from the contract date — 15 days is the common window, and some states run it from the first application instead.
Set the event SLA to the state window minus 5 days so a rejected transaction can be re-submitted inside the window.
checklist.done: one appointment event exists per requested state with the statutory clock started from the contract date and an SLA set inside the window.

checklist.step: Verify the underlying licence and variable authority before appointing
actions: In the NIPR Gateway run a Producer Database inquiry on the national producer number and read the licence status, class, lines of authority and expiry per state.
Confirm the state licence carries life and variable life or variable annuity authority — a life-only licence cannot support variable business.
Read the regulatory action and administrative action sections and route any hit to the Producer Compliance Manager before appointing.
For securities business confirm the Series 6 or 7 registration is active in that state in CRD.
Attach the dated PDB inquiry to the event as the pre-appointment evidence.
checklist.done: a dated PDB inquiry on the event shows an active licence with variable authority and no unresolved regulatory action.

checklist.step: Transact the appointment through NIPR and record the confirmation
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ New Appointment, select the state, the appointing company by NAIC code and the lines of authority.
Submit the transaction with the appointment effective date and pay the state appointment fee through the gateway account.
Read the transaction response the same day — rejections for licence class mismatch or unpaid fees must be corrected and re-submitted inside the state window.
Post the confirmation number and effective date back onto the producer record and release the producer code for that state only from the effective date.
checklist.done: every requested state shows a NIPR appointment confirmation number and the producer code is released only from the effective date.

checklist.step: Block solicitation and submission before the appointment is effective
actions: Feed the appointment effective dates by producer and state from the producer management system into the new-business authority table nightly.
Configure the submission rule to reject any application whose signed date precedes the producer's appointment effective date in the application state.
Configure the commission rule to hold, not pay, commission on any application that bypasses the check pending a compliance decision.
Test the block quarterly with a deliberately back-dated test application and confirm the rejection message names the producer and state.
checklist.done: the system rejects applications signed before the producer's appointment effective date, proven by a quarterly test rejection.

checklist.step: File or amend the Form U4 for securities-registered producers
actions: In FINRA Gateway open Forms ▸ U4 and file the registration request for the requested states and categories, or the amendment for a transfer.

For a disclosable event — customer complaint, judgment, lien, criminal charge, regulatory action — file the amendment within 30 days of the firm learning of the fact and record the learning date on the event.
Read the CRD response for deficiencies and clear each one before the 30-day clock expires.
Attach the filing acknowledgement and the day count to the producer record.
checklist.done: each U4 filing or amendment is acknowledged in CRD with a recorded learning date and a day count inside 30 days.

checklist.step: Refresh the Firm Element covered-person roster on every joiner and transfer
actions: Push the new or transferred registered person to the covered-person roster within 2 business days of the registration approval date.
Assign the current year's Firm Element curriculum, plus the Rule 2330(e) deferred variable annuity training where the person will sell VAs, with a due date 30 days from assignment.
Assign the new supervising principal the supervisory modules for the products the transferred person sells.
Confirm the LMS assignment exists before the producer code is released for variable business.
checklist.done: every joiner and transfer is on the covered-person roster with assigned training before their producer code is released for variable business.

checklist.step: Open a termination event the day notice is given or the decision is made
actions: Raise the termination in Workday with the last day of employment or the contract termination date and the reason code.
Push the event to the producer management system the same day, flagged voluntary, involuntary or for cause.

Where the reason touches conduct — a customer complaint, a compliance failure, a suspected misappropriation — route it to Employment Counsel and the Producer Compliance Manager before any language is drafted.
Start the 30-day U5 clock and the state termination-notice clocks from the termination date.
checklist.done: a termination event exists with a reason classification, both clocks started, and conduct cases routed to counsel the same day.

checklist.step: Agree the Form U5 termination language before filing
actions: Draft the reason-for-termination narrative to be accurate, complete and not misleading, using the facts on record rather than settlement-negotiated wording.
Complete the U5 disclosure questions on internal review for fraud, wrongful taking of property or violation of investment-related statutes, and answer them on the evidence held.
Where an internal investigation is open at the termination date, record it and diarise the amended U5 for within 30 days of the investigation concluding.
Sign off the language in writing and hand it to the Producer Licensing Coordinator for filing.
checklist.done: counsel has signed off the U5 reason narrative and disclosure answers, with any open investigation diarised for an amended U5.

checklist.step: File the Form U5 and send the copy to the producer
actions: In FINRA Gateway open Forms ▸ U5, file full termination with the termination date and the approved reason and disclosure answers, within 30 days of the termination date.
Send a copy of the filed U5 to the former producer at their last known residential address and record the despatch date and channel.
File any amended U5 within 30 days of learning facts that change a disclosure answer.
Record the CRD acknowledgement, the filing date and the recomputed day count on the termination event.
checklist.done: the U5 is filed inside 30 days, a copy is evidenced as sent to the producer, and the day count is recorded.

checklist.step: File the state appointment terminations through NIPR
actions: In the NIPR Gateway open Appointments ▸ Termination and submit a termination for every state in which the producer was appointed for the terminating company.
Select the correct termination reason code — states distinguish voluntary from cause, and a cause code triggers state reporting obligations.
Meet each state's window, commonly 30 days from the termination date, and record the confirmation number per state.
Where a state requires a separate written notice to the producer or the department, generate and send it and file the proof.
checklist.done: every appointed state has a NIPR termination confirmation with the correct reason code inside the state window.

checklist.step: Stop production access, commissions and system entitlements
actions: Deactivate the producer code for new business on the termination date and record the deactivation timestamp.
Move renewal and trail commissions to the contract's post-termination treatment and place any disputed amount on hold.
Raise the access removal ticket for the broker portal, the illustration tool and email on the termination date and confirm closure within 24 hours.
Reassign the orphaned in-force book to a servicing producer and notify affected policyholders in writing.
checklist.done: the producer code is deactivated on the termination date, entitlements are removed within 24 hours and the book is reassigned.

checklist.step: Remove the leaver from the covered-person roster and close training
actions: Remove the leaver from the covered-person roster within 2 business days of termination so completion statistics are not distorted.
Archive the transcript rather than deleting it — the training record must survive the 6-year retention period.
Where the person transferred rather than left, retain them on the roster and re-assign training to the new supervisor's population.
Reconcile the roster headcount to CRD and HRIS after the month's events are processed.
checklist.done: leavers are off the roster with archived transcripts and the roster reconciles to CRD and HRIS at month end.

checklist.step: Work the SLA breach queue daily
actions: Run the event ageing report each morning showing every open appointment, termination, U4 and U5 event with days elapsed against its statutory window.
Chase the named owner for anything at day 20 of a 30-day clock or day 10 of a 15-day clock.
Escalate to the Producer Compliance Manager at day 25 and to the Head of Compliance at day 28.
Record the daily queue position and the escalations so the ageing history survives the event closing.
checklist.done: no event passes its penultimate escalation point without a recorded chase, and the daily ageing history is retained.

checklist.step: Escalate and remediate pre-appointment business and late filings
actions: Take the weekly report of applications signed before the producer's appointment effective date and of U4 and U5 filings beyond 30 days.
For pre-appointment business, quantify the policies, premium and states affected and decide with Regulatory Counsel whether a state notification is required.
Raise a GRC exception per case with the producer number, the state, the day count and the root cause, and assign a remediation owner and date.
Sign the disposition personally and record whether commission was clawed back or released.
checklist.done: every pre-appointment case and late filing has a quantified impact, a signed disposition and a dated remediation owner.

checklist.step: Retain the event evidence for the retention period
actions: File per producer: the contract, PDB inquiry, NIPR appointment and termination confirmations, U4 and U5 filings with acknowledgements, the U5 despatch proof and the roster entries, under REG-014-C13.
Apply the 6-year retention label per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4, extended where a state record rule is longer.
Confirm the record is searchable by national producer number, CRD number, state and event date.
Record the retention expiry on the index entry.
checklist.done: each producer event file is complete, labelled for at least 6-year retention and searchable by producer number and state.

testing.step: Build the population of appointment, transfer and termination events
actions: Extract every appointment, transfer and termination event in the quarter with producer number, state, contract date, effective date, filing date and owner.
Extract independently the Workday joiner and leaver list and the CRD registration and de-registration history for the same period.
Add the NIPR appointment and termination confirmation extract for the appointing companies.
Sign the extract with the run date and record row counts for each source before sampling.
testing.done: a dated, signed event population from the producer system, HRIS, CRD and NIPR exists with per-source row counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the event population to HRIS, CRD and NIPR
actions: Match every Workday leaver to a termination event and a filed U5, and every joiner to an appointment event.
Match every NIPR appointment and termination confirmation to an event record and list confirmations with no event — an appointment transacted outside the process is a control bypass.
Compare the CRD registration history to the event dates and list registrations with no matching internal event.
Resolve or log every difference before sampling and record the reconciled counts.
testing.done: every HRIS, CRD and NIPR record matches an event or is logged, with reconciled counts recorded in the workpaper.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of for-cause terminations and 100% of events that breached an SLA alert during the quarter.
Take 40 further events at random on a recorded seed, stratified across appointments, transfers and terminations and across states.
Add 100% of producers with any application signed within 10 days of their appointment effective date, where a timing error is most likely.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers all for-cause terminations, all SLA breaches and all near-boundary appointments.

testing.step: Re-perform the pre-appointment licence verification in NIPR
actions: For each sampled appointment run a Producer Database inquiry on the national producer number and read the licence class, lines of authority and status history.
Confirm the licence with variable authority was in force in that state on the appointment effective date, working from the licence history rather than today's status.
Compare to the PDB inquiry the coordinator attached — a missing or undated attachment is an exception even where the licence was valid.
Read the regulatory action section and confirm any hit present at appointment was escalated before the appointment was transacted.
Capture the PDB screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled appointment has an independent PDB re-performance proving variable authority on the effective date, captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Trace each appointment to a NIPR confirmation and each termination to a state notice
actions: Search the recorded NIPR confirmation number for each sampled event and confirm the state, company NAIC code, lines of authority and effective date match the internal record.
For terminations confirm a termination transaction exists for every state in which the producer was appointed for that company, not only the home state.
Read the termination reason code and compare it to the internal classification — a for-cause termination filed as voluntary is a reportable exception.
Capture each confirmation screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled event traces to a NIPR confirmation matching the internal record, with termination reason codes verified.

testing.step: Test for business written before the appointment effective date
actions: Extract every application in the quarter with its signed date, application state and writing producer number.
Join to the appointment effective dates and list every application signed before the producer's effective date in that state.
For each hit read the application image to confirm the signed date rather than relying on the keyed field.
Quantify premium and policy count per hit and confirm each was reported to the Head of Compliance in the week it arose.
testing.done: every application signed before its producer's appointment effective date is identified from source images and quantified.

testing.step: Trace U4 and U5 filings to CRD acknowledgements and to the producer copy
actions: In FINRA Gateway open the filing history for each sampled producer and read the U4 or U5 filing date, the form version and the disclosure answers as filed.
Compare the filed reason narrative to the counsel-approved language and treat any unapproved edit as an exception.
Confirm the U5 copy despatch to the former producer is evidenced with a date and channel.
Where an internal investigation was open at termination, confirm the amended U5 was filed within 30 days of its conclusion.
Capture the CRD filing detail screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: every sampled U4 and U5 traces to a CRD acknowledgement matching the approved language, with the producer copy evidenced.

testing.step: Recompute every statutory day count
actions: Recompute U5 filing date minus termination date and test against 30 days; recompute amended U5 date minus the learning date on the same basis.
Recompute U4 amendment date minus the date the firm learned of the disclosable fact, taking the learning date from the complaint or court document rather than the internal case record.
Recompute NIPR appointment date minus contract date, and termination date minus the state window, per state, using each state's own window rather than a single assumed 30 days.
Compute the quarter's late-filing rate and compare it to the 2% threshold.
testing.done: every statutory day count is independently recomputed from source dates and the quarter's late-filing rate is measured against 2%.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the producer number, the state, the event, the day count and the rule or statute breached.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: contract received late by licensing, PDB check skipped, NIPR rejection not re-worked, learning date recorded late, wrong termination reason code, state window assumed rather than looked up.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and for pre-appointment business require a state notification decision from Regulatory Counsel within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue reference, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the pre-appointment business count to the zero-tolerance threshold and the late-filing rate to the 2% threshold.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the workpaper references and any state notification opened.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Licensing Operations and filed none of the sampled transactions, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the pre-appointment count and the late-filing rate, and is filed with a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the renewal calendar across three cycles — the FINRA Renewal Program for firm and individual registrations, state insurance licence renewals through NIPR, and the annual Regulatory Element and Firm Element continuing education deadlines

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA Rule 1240(a) (Regulatory Element, annual, by December 31) and Rule 1240(b) (Firm Element) read in the FINRA rulebook alongside the current-year FINRA Renewal Program notice, plus each state's licence renewal period and CE hour requirement including the annuity and long-term care training rules

In-scope processes.value: Annual renewal cycle for the broker-dealer and every registered person, state insurance licence renewals by birth-month or biennial cycle, Regulatory Element completion by December 31, Firm Element completion by December 31, and state CE hour tracking including annuity suitability training

In-scope systems.value: State licence renewals and CE transcripts through the NIPR Gateway and Producer Database; FINRA renewals through the E-Bill Preliminary and Final Statements; Regulatory Element completed in FinPro and Firm Element delivered in the LMS

Compliance procedure documented.value: Licence Renewal and Continuing Education Procedure — the renewal calendar build, the FINRA Preliminary Statement reconciliation and payment, state renewal batching by cycle, CE hour tracking with the annuity-training carve-out, and the lapse-prevention escalation ladder

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance before the renewal season opens each September; re-approved on any change to the FINRA renewal timetable or a state CE requirement published in a bulletin

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: FINRA Preliminary Statement issued in mid-November with payment due by the stated December date, Final Statement issued in early January; Regulatory Element and Firm Element both complete by December 31; state licence renewals by each state's expiry, with state CE hours completed before the renewal is transacted

Deadline reminders configured.value: Renewal calendar alerts at T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-10 days to each state expiry and to December 31 for CE; a dedicated escalation on the FINRA payment due date, since non-payment moves registrations to failed-to-renew

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Preliminary and Final Statements with the reconciliation and payment confirmation, NIPR renewal confirmations, CE transcripts from the Producer Database and the LMS, and the lapse exception log retained 6 years per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4, and per state rules where longer

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every lapsed licence, failed-to-renew registration, CE deficiency at December 31 and missed state CE hour requirement is logged with the producer number, the state, the lapse period, any business written during the lapse and a dated reinstatement plan

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off the reinstatement plan for every lapse and personally clears the release of any producer code after a lapse is cured

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every registered person and appointed producer with a renewal or CE deadline falling in the cycle, taken from the FINRA Preliminary Statement, the NIPR Producer Database licence expiry extract and the covered-person roster

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on business written under a lapsed licence or a failed-to-renew registration; CE completion must reach 100% by December 31 and any state licence allowed to lapse is a fail regardless of whether business was written

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation runs on an annual renewal cycle with rolling state expiries; the test runs in January over the completed cycle and again at each quarter end over that quarter's state expiries

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in Licensing Operations and must not have transacted any sampled renewal or CE credit posting

Evidence location for test results.value: Annual renewal and CE workpaper (Preliminary Statement reconciliation, licence expiry population, sample with seed, PDB re-performance, lapse day counts, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C14

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Preliminary and Final Statement reconciliation with payment proof, per-state renewal confirmations, per-person CE transcripts and the lapse register, producible for a state market conduct exam or a FINRA cycle exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers state department licence and CE inquiries and FINRA renewal queries; Regulatory Counsel clears any admission that business was written during a lapse before it is sent

checklist.step: Build the renewal calendar for the coming cycle
actions: Extract from the NIPR Producer Database every appointed producer's licence expiry date, renewal cycle and state CE due date, by state.
Extract from CRD every registered person with their Regulatory Element anniversary and their registration states.
Load both into the renewal calendar with one row per person per state per obligation, and set the alert schedule at T-90, T-60, T-30 and T-10 days.
Publish the calendar to Distribution Operations and the branch principals in September so producers know their own dates.
checklist.done: the renewal calendar holds a dated row per person, per state and per obligation, published before the season opens.

checklist.step: Reconcile the FINRA Preliminary Statement line by line
actions: Download the Preliminary Statement from FINRA E-Bill when it issues in mid-November and export the individual and branch renewal detail.
Match every billed individual to the current CRD roster and to Workday active employment; list anyone billed who has left and anyone employed who is not billed.
Match every billed state registration to the states the person actually needs, and remove registrations the firm no longer requires by filing the U4 amendment before the payment date.
Confirm the branch office count on the statement matches the branch register and the Form BD.
checklist.done: every Preliminary Statement line is matched to an active person, a needed state or a real branch, with differences resolved before payment.

checklist.step: Pay the FINRA renewal assessment before the due date
actions: Raise the payment against the reconciled Preliminary Statement total, coded to the regulatory fees account, at least 5 business days before the stated December due date.
Fund the FINRA Flex-Funding account through E-Bill by ACH and confirm the funds show as available, since a scheduled but unsettled transfer does not count as payment.
Send the payment confirmation and the E-Bill receipt to the Producer Licensing Coordinator the same day.
Flag any shortfall against the statement total immediately — an underpayment moves registrations to failed-to-renew on January 1.
checklist.done: the reconciled renewal total is paid and settled in the Flex-Funding account before the FINRA due date, with a receipt on file.

checklist.step: Check the Final Statement and clear every failed-to-renew item
actions: Download the Final Statement from E-Bill in early January and compare it to the Preliminary reconciliation.
List every registration showing failed-to-renew or terminated and establish the cause — underpayment, late U4 amendment, or a state that requires a separate action.
Restore each affected registration immediately by paying the balance or filing the required form, and record the date the registration returned to approved.
Suspend the producer code of anyone whose registration is not approved on January 1 until it is restored.
checklist.done: the Final Statement is reconciled, every failed-to-renew registration has a dated restoration, and unapproved producers are suspended.

checklist.step: Track Regulatory Element completion to December 31
actions: Pull the Regulatory Element status for every registered person from FINRA Gateway and identify anyone showing incomplete for the current calendar year.
Send each person their FinPro link and their deadline, and copy their supervising principal with the named list.
Report weekly from October 1 by branch, naming individuals rather than reporting percentages.
Escalate anyone still incomplete at December 10 to the Head of Compliance, since a person who does not complete by December 31 becomes CE-inactive.
checklist.done: a weekly named Regulatory Element status report runs from October 1 and every December 10 non-completer is escalated.

checklist.step: Track Firm Element completion against the annual plan
actions: Run the LMS completion report against the year's covered-person roster and the plan's course list, filtered to Not Started and In Progress.
Confirm the roster used for assignments is the current one — a producer appointed in October must carry the year's assignments.
Reconcile the LMS completion count to the CRD registered headcount and explain every difference before year end.
Escalate the named non-completers to the Producer Compliance Manager at T-30 and to the Head of Compliance at T-10 days to December 31.
checklist.done: Firm Element completion is tracked against the current roster, reconciled to CRD headcount and escalated on the T-30 and T-10 ladder.

checklist.step: Track state insurance CE hours including the annuity training carve-out
actions: Pull each producer's CE transcript from the state CE tracking service through the Producer Database and compare hours earned to the state requirement, typically 24 hours per biennium with an ethics component.
Test separately for the state's one-time annuity suitability training and any product-specific training required before selling a carrier's annuity, and for long-term care training where applicable.
List producers short of hours with the deficit by category and send it to them and their agency manager at T-90 days to the licence expiry.
Confirm credits post to the state transcript, not only to the LMS — a completed course that has not posted will not renew the licence.
checklist.done: every producer's state CE position is measured by category against the state requirement with credits confirmed as posted to the state transcript.

checklist.step: Transact the state licence renewals through NIPR
actions: Batch the month's expiring licences by state and open the NIPR Gateway licence renewal transaction for each state's window.
Submit the renewal with the fee and read the response the same day; correct CE-deficiency and unpaid-fee rejections and re-submit inside the window.
Where the state requires the producer to renew personally, send the producer the state link, the deadline and the fee, and chase weekly until the Producer Database shows renewed.
Post the renewal confirmation and the new expiry date to the producer record and the renewal calendar.
checklist.done: every expiring licence is renewed inside its window with a NIPR confirmation and a refreshed expiry date on the calendar.

checklist.step: Renew the company appointments that follow the state renewal cycle
actions: Identify the states that bill appointment renewals annually or biennially and pull the state's appointment renewal invoice through the gateway.
Reconcile the billed appointment list to the producers the firm still wants appointed, and terminate the appointments of leavers before paying rather than after.
Pay the renewal within the state window and record the confirmation per state.
Refresh the authority table in the policy administration system with the renewed appointment dates.
checklist.done: appointment renewals are reconciled to the active producer list, paid inside the window and reflected in the authority table.

checklist.step: Run the lapse-prevention escalation ladder
actions: Run the calendar exception report daily showing every obligation inside 30 days of its deadline and not yet complete.

At T-30 send the producer and their agency manager the named deficit; at T-10 escalate to the Producer Compliance Manager; at T-3 escalate to the Head of Compliance with the proposed producer-code suspension.
Record every contact with its date and channel so the chase history survives the deadline.
Never close a row on a verbal assurance — close only on a NIPR confirmation, a CRD status or a posted CE credit.
checklist.done: every deadline inside 30 days is chased on the T-30, T-10, T-3 ladder and closed only on system evidence.

checklist.step: Suspend production immediately on any lapse
actions: Take the daily lapse feed from the producer management system and deactivate the affected producer code for the affected state the same day.
Hold commission on any pending application from that producer in the affected state pending the compliance review.
Notify the producer, their agency manager and the branch principal in writing that they may not solicit in that state until reinstatement.
Reassign any in-flight cases to an appointed producer rather than letting them sit.
checklist.done: every lapse suspends the producer code in the affected state the same day, with commission held and cases reassigned.

checklist.step: Reinstate lapsed licences and quantify any business written during the lapse
actions: Establish the exact lapse period from the Producer Database licence history — the expiry date and the reinstatement date.
Extract every application signed and every policy issued in that state with that producer number inside the lapse period, with premium and policy count.
Complete the state's reinstatement route — late renewal with penalty, or a fresh application where the reinstatement window has closed — and record the confirmation.
Route any business written during the lapse to Regulatory Counsel for a commission-disgorgement and state-notification decision.
checklist.done: each lapse has a measured period, a quantified business impact and a completed reinstatement with a state confirmation.

checklist.step: Close out the cycle and report the results
actions: Produce the January cycle report: renewal population, on-time renewal rate, failed-to-renew count and cure time, CE completion rate at December 31 and the lapse register with business impact.
State the root causes of the cycle's lapses and the process change made for the next cycle.
Table the report at the Compliance Committee and record the directions given.
Feed the lessons into the September procedure refresh for the next season.
checklist.done: a cycle report with on-time rates, lapse register and named process changes is tabled at the Compliance Committee.

checklist.step: Log lapses and CE deficiencies as exceptions with owners
actions: Raise a GRC exception per lapse or CE deficiency naming the producer number, the state, the lapse period and the business written during it.
Assign a root cause from the fixed list: credit not posted to the state transcript, renewal fee unpaid, producer self-renewal not completed, FINRA payment short, calendar row missing.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and, where business was written, require the counsel decision within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
checklist.done: every lapse and CE deficiency carries an issue reference, a root cause, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

checklist.step: Retain the renewal and CE evidence for the retention period
actions: File the Preliminary and Final Statements with the reconciliation and payment receipts, the NIPR renewal confirmations, the CE transcripts and the lapse register under REG-014-C14 and the cycle year.
Apply the 6-year retention label per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4, extended where a state record rule is longer.
Confirm the record is searchable by national producer number, CRD number, state and expiry date.
Record the retention expiry on the index entry.
checklist.done: the cycle evidence is filed, labelled for at least 6-year retention and searchable by producer number, state and expiry date.

testing.step: Build the population of renewal and CE obligations for the cycle
actions: Extract from the NIPR Producer Database every appointed producer with a licence expiry falling in the cycle, by state.
Extract from CRD every registered person with a Regulatory Element obligation and every state registration billed on the FINRA Preliminary Statement.
Add the covered-person roster used for Firm Element assignment at the year end.
Sign the extract with the run date and record row counts per source before sampling.
testing.done: a dated, signed population of licence expiries, registrations and CE obligations exists with per-source row counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the FINRA statements and to HRIS
actions: Match every Preliminary Statement individual line to an active person in Workday and to a CRD registration, and list every billed leaver and every unbilled active registered person.
Compare the Preliminary Statement total to the payment amount settled in the Flex-Funding account and to the Final Statement.
Compare the covered-person roster to the CRD registered headcount at December 31 and explain every difference.
Resolve or log every difference before sampling and record the reconciled counts.
testing.done: the statement, payment, CRD roster and HRIS headcount reconcile, with every difference explained or logged.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of producers who lapsed or were failed-to-renew at any point in the cycle.
Take 40 producers at random on a recorded seed, stratified across states and across annual and biennial renewal cycles.
Add 100% of producers whose CE credits posted in the final 10 days before their deadline, where posting failures concentrate.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers all lapses and all late-posting CE cases.

testing.step: Re-perform the licence status check in the Producer Database
actions: Run a Producer Database inquiry for each sampled producer and read the licence history: expiry date, renewal date, status and lines of authority per state.
Confirm the licence was continuously in force across the cycle and that variable authority persisted through the renewal.
Compare the PDB history to the internal renewal calendar and treat any internal record showing renewed where PDB shows lapsed as a data-integrity exception.
Capture the PDB licence history screen into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled producer's licence continuity is independently proven from the PDB history and captured in the workpaper.

testing.step: Re-perform the CE hour computation against the state requirement
actions: Pull each sampled producer's state CE transcript and total the credits by category — general, ethics, annuity suitability, long-term care.
Look up the state's requirement independently from the department's CE page rather than from the internal reference table, and compare category by category.
Confirm the annuity suitability training was completed before the producer's first annuity sale, not merely before the renewal.
Treat credits recorded in the LMS but absent from the state transcript as not earned.
testing.done: each sampled producer's CE position is recomputed by category from the state transcript against an independently sourced requirement.

testing.step: Trace Regulatory and Firm Element completion to system records
actions: Open the FINRA Gateway CE status for each sampled registered person and read the Regulatory Element completion date for the calendar year.
Open the LMS transcript and confirm every Firm Element course on the year's plan for that person's population shows Complete with a date on or before December 31.
Confirm the person was on the covered-person roster used for assignment — an unassigned person cannot be counted as compliant.
Export both records into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled person's Regulatory and Firm Element completion is traced to Gateway and LMS records dated on or before December 31.

testing.step: Test whether business was written during any lapse
actions: For every lapsed producer take the exact lapse window from the PDB history and extract applications signed and policies issued in that state and window.
Read the application images to confirm the signed dates rather than relying on the keyed field.
Quantify premium, policy count and commission paid inside each lapse window.
Confirm each case was escalated to Regulatory Counsel and that a disgorgement or notification decision is on file.
testing.done: business written in every lapse window is quantified from source images with a counsel decision evidenced.

testing.step: Recompute the renewal and CE deadline maths
actions: Recompute renewal transaction date minus licence expiry date per sampled state and list every renewal transacted after expiry.
Recompute the FINRA payment settlement date against the stated December due date and confirm settlement, not merely instruction, preceded it.
Recompute CE completion date minus December 31 for every sampled registered person and minus the licence expiry for state CE.
Compute the cycle's on-time renewal rate and the CE completion rate and compare them to the 100% threshold.
testing.done: every renewal, payment and CE day count is independently recomputed and the cycle's on-time and completion rates are measured.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the producer number, the state, the obligation, the day count and the business impact.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: calendar row missing, CE credit never posted to the state, renewal fee unpaid, producer self-renewal not completed, FINRA payment settled late, roster stale at assignment.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and, for any business written during a lapse, require the counsel decision within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the next cycle's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue reference, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the lapse count and the CE completion rate to the zero-lapse and 100% thresholds and quantify any business written under a lapsed licence.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Licensing Operations and transacted no sampled renewal, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the lapse count and the CE completion rate, and is filed with a committee reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the pre-registration screening gate for every associated person — fingerprint submission under SEA Rule 17f-2, the Rule 3110(e) background investigation, the statutory disqualification review and the 18 U.S.C. 1033 written consent for anyone engaged in the business of insurance

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — SEA Rule 17f-2 (fingerprinting of securities industry personnel) and FINRA Rule 3110(e) (responsibility of member to investigate applicants for registration) read in the current SEC and FINRA rulebooks, together with Exchange Act 3(a)(39), FINRA By-Laws Article III Section 3(b) and 18 U.S.C. 1033/1034 for the insurance-side consent

In-scope processes.value: Pre-hire and pre-contract screening for registered representatives, principals, and non-registered fingerprintable persons with access to customer funds, securities or the books and records — from offer acceptance through fingerprint clearance, background investigation, disqualification review and U4 filing

In-scope systems.value: Candidate pipeline and offer stage gates in the recruiting system; screening orders and results in the vendor platform; fingerprints submitted electronically to FINRA for FBI processing through the fingerprint vendor; results read back in CRD

Compliance procedure documented.value: Pre-Registration Screening Procedure — fingerprintable-person determination, electronic fingerprint submission and rejection handling, the Rule 3110(e) investigation scope, the 3-year employment and 10-year residence verification, the 1033 consent, and the statutory disqualification decision route

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with Employment Counsel concurrence on the FCRA and adverse-action steps; re-approved annually and on any change to Rule 3110(e) or the SEC fingerprint requirements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Fingerprints submitted before the person begins fingerprintable functions and in any event promptly on U4 filing; the Rule 3110(e) background investigation completed and the Form U4 verified no later than 30 calendar days after the U4 is filed; a rejected fingerprint print resubmitted immediately, with the second rejection routed to the FBI name-check alternative

Deadline reminders configured.value: Recruiting workflow alerts at day 10, 20 and 25 of the 30-day Rule 3110(e) verification clock; a daily alert on any fingerprint submitted more than 5 business days ago without a returned result, and an immediate alert on any rejected print

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Fingerprint submission and FBI result records retained for at least 3 years after termination per SEA Rule 17f-2(d), and the investigation file — verification evidence, public records search, 1033 consent and the disqualification memo — retained 6 years per FINRA Rule 4511 and SEA Rule 17a-4

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Any person who performed fingerprintable functions before a cleared fingerprint, any Rule 3110(e) verification completed beyond 30 days, and any missing 1033 consent is logged with the candidate, the start date, the day count and a dated remediation owner

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs off every case where a person started before clearance, including the decision to suspend access, and clears every adverse screening result before the registration proceeds

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: Every associated person who joined, was contracted, or was newly registered in the quarter, taken from the recruiting system and Workday and reconciled to CRD U4 filings and to the fingerprint submission log

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on a person performing fingerprintable functions before a cleared fingerprint result or a documented exemption; any Rule 3110(e) verification completed beyond 30 days of U4 filing is a fail, and any missing 1033 consent blocks insurance activity outright

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The obligation is per hire and continuous; the test runs quarterly over that quarter's hire and contract population, with an immediate targeted test on any adverse screening result or statutory disqualification case

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must sit outside Compliance Operations and HR and must not have performed or approved any sampled screening

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly pre-registration screening workpaper (hire population, CRD and fingerprint reconciliation, sample with seed, verification re-performance, day-count recomputation, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C15

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Per-person screening file — signed 1033 consent and FCRA authorisation, fingerprint submission and result, employment and residence verification evidence, public records search, disqualification memo and the U4 — producible for a FINRA cycle exam within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Head of Compliance answers FINRA Rule 8210 requests on registration investigations; Employment Counsel handles the individual-facing FCRA adverse-action process and Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of an unfingerprinted person before it is sent

checklist.step: Decide at offer stage whether the role is registered and fingerprintable
actions: At offer acceptance open the requisition and set the compliance classification: registered representative, registered principal, non-registered fingerprintable, or out of scope.

Classify as fingerprintable under SEA Rule 17f-2 anyone who will be engaged in the sale of securities, regularly have access to securities, monies or the original books and records, or supervise those who do.
Take the hiring manager's written description of the actual duties rather than relying on the job title, and attach it to the candidate record.
Set the start date gate so onboarding cannot complete until the screening stage is marked cleared.
checklist.done: the candidate record carries a documented fingerprintable and registration classification supported by a written duty description.

checklist.step: Capture the consents and authorisations before any search is ordered
actions: Send the candidate the packet: FCRA disclosure and written authorisation on a standalone document, the Rule 3110(e) authorisation to verify employment, education and regulatory history, and the 18 U.S.C. 1033 written consent for insurance activity.
Include the Form U4 Item 14 disclosure questionnaire and the residence history covering the last 10 years and employment history covering the last 10 years with no unexplained gaps over 3 months.
Refuse to order any search until the executed packet is returned — an order without the standalone FCRA authorisation is itself a violation.
File the executed envelope certificate and each signed document to the screening file.
checklist.done: the screening file holds an executed FCRA authorisation, Rule 3110(e) authorisation, 1033 consent and a gap-free 10-year history.

checklist.step: Submit fingerprints and clear rejections
actions: Book the candidate at an approved electronic fingerprint vendor site and give them the firm's CRD number and the FINRA ORI so the prints route to FINRA for FBI processing.
Submit before the person begins any fingerprintable function; record the submission date and the transaction control number on the screening file.
Monitor the fingerprint results in CRD and re-submit immediately on a rejection for print quality — the clock does not restart the person's start-date gate.
After a second rejection, submit the FBI name-check alternative permitted for unclassifiable prints and record the reason on the file.
Read the returned FBI response and route any criminal history entry to Regulatory Counsel the same day.
checklist.done: a fingerprint result or a documented name-check alternative is on file, submitted before the person performed any fingerprintable function.

checklist.step: Search CRD and BrokerCheck for the applicant's regulatory history
actions: In FINRA Gateway open CRD ▸ Individual Search and pull the Individual Snapshot, the Disclosure report and every prior Form U5.
Read each prior U5 reason for termination and each disclosure event, and compare them line by line to the candidate's questionnaire answers.
Run BrokerCheck separately and compare, since a discrepancy between the two indicates an unamended filing.
List every difference on the screening file and require a written explanation from the candidate before proceeding.
checklist.done: dated CRD and BrokerCheck extracts are on file with every difference against the questionnaire explained in writing.

checklist.step: Run the public records and criminal searches
actions: Order the Rule 3110(e) public records package: national and county criminal searches covering every county of residence for 7 years, federal district court search, civil judgments and liens, bankruptcy, and OFAC and global sanctions screening.
Order the credit report where the role involves handling customer funds or the firm's books and records, using the FCRA authorisation already captured.
Require the underlying court record for any hit rather than accepting the vendor summary, and attach it to the file.
Record the search date, the scope covered and the vendor reference on the screening file.
checklist.done: a completed public records package covering criminal, civil, bankruptcy and sanctions is on file with court records behind every hit.

checklist.step: Verify employment, education and residence independently
actions: Contact each employer for the last 3 years directly and record the contact name, date, dates of employment and the stated reason for leaving.
Verify the highest qualification claimed with the awarding institution and record the verification reference.
Verify the 10-year residence history against the public records address trail and challenge any address the candidate did not disclose.
Where an employer refuses to confirm, record the refusal and obtain a secondary source — a payslip, tax record or W-2 — rather than leaving the period unverified.
checklist.done: every employment period in the last 3 years, the claimed qualification and the 10-year address trail are verified from an independent source.

checklist.step: Reconcile the verification results against the Form U4 before filing
actions: Lay the completed U4 against the verified employment history and confirm the dates, employers and gaps match exactly.
Confirm every disclosure event found in CRD, the public records search or the FBI response is answered Yes on the U4 with a completed disclosure reporting page.
Correct the U4 before filing rather than filing and amending; a knowingly inaccurate U4 is itself a disciplinary matter.
Record the reconciliation and the reviewer on the screening file, and file the U4 with the CRD acknowledgement attached.
checklist.done: the U4 as filed matches the verified history and every discovered disclosure event, with the reconciliation recorded and signed.

checklist.step: Complete the Rule 3110(e) investigation inside 30 days of the U4 filing
actions: Track the 30-calendar-day clock from the U4 filing date and confirm every verification component is complete and evidenced before it expires.
Where the applicant was registered with another firm in the last 5 years, review the most recent Form U5 obtained from that firm within 60 days of the U4 filing, and compare it to the U4 answers.
Write the investigation conclusion memo naming each source used, what it showed and why the applicant is fit to register.
Sign and date the memo — an unsigned memo does not satisfy the rule.
checklist.done: a signed Rule 3110(e) investigation memo dated within 30 days of the U4 filing names every source and its result.

checklist.step: Decide statutory disqualification before the person acts
actions: Test the FBI response and every disclosure against Exchange Act 3(a)(39) and FINRA By-Laws Article III Section 3(b): felonies and specified misdemeanours within 10 years, regulator or SRO bars and suspensions, injunctions and false application statements.

Test the insurance side against 18 U.S.C. 1033 — a conviction involving dishonesty or breach of trust bars the person from the business of insurance without written consent from the state commissioner.
Where disqualification exists, block the start date and open the MC-400 eligibility proceeding, and separately apply for the state 1033 written consent.
Record the conclusion, the limbs tested and any heightened supervision conditions in a signed memo on the screening file.
checklist.done: a signed memo tests every disqualification limb on both the securities and insurance sides and records any MC-400 or 1033 consent opened.

checklist.step: Run the FCRA adverse-action process where a report drives a decision
actions: Where a consumer report contributes to a decision to withdraw an offer, send the pre-adverse-action notice with a copy of the report and the Summary of Rights.
Allow the candidate a reasonable period — 5 business days is the working standard — to dispute the accuracy before any final decision.
Send the final adverse-action notice naming the reporting agency and the candidate's right to a free report and to dispute.
Record both notices with their despatch dates on the screening file, kept separately from the fitness conclusion.
checklist.done: both FCRA notices are evidenced with despatch dates and a dispute window was allowed before the final decision.

checklist.step: Hold the start date until the screening gate clears
actions: Keep the Workday onboarding step blocked until Compliance marks the screening cleared, and confirm system access provisioning is chained to that step.

Where the business needs the person to start before the fingerprint result returns, restrict them in writing from all fingerprintable functions — no securities access, no customer funds, no original books and records — and evidence the restriction.
Confirm with IT that entitlements to the brokerage, policy administration and document systems are withheld while the restriction stands.
Release the restriction only on a written clearance from the Compliance Officer.
checklist.done: no person performs fingerprintable functions before clearance, and any early start carries an evidenced, IT-enforced restriction.

checklist.step: Screen contracted producers and third-party distributors to the same standard
actions: Apply the same gate to independent producers and agency principals contracted to sell the firm's variable products before any appointment is transacted.
