Run the Producer Database regulatory action and administrative action sections and the state department disciplinary lookups for each contracting state.
Obtain the 1033 written consent and, where the producer is registered with a different broker-dealer, confirm that firm's fingerprint and investigation coverage in writing.
Record the screening conclusion on the producer record before the appointment event is opened.
checklist.done: no producer contract or appointment opens without a completed screening conclusion on the producer record.

checklist.step: Work the screening exception queue daily
actions: Run the daily report of fingerprints submitted more than 5 business days ago with no result, U4 filings past day 20 of the 30-day investigation clock, and any started person with an incomplete file.
Chase the named owner on each row and escalate to the Compliance Officer at day 25 of the 30-day clock.
Raise a GRC exception the moment a person is found to have performed a fingerprintable function before clearance and suspend their access the same day.
Record the daily queue position so the ageing history survives the file closing.
checklist.done: every open screening item is chased daily and any pre-clearance function triggers a same-day access suspension and exception.

checklist.step: Re-screen on trigger events during employment
actions: Re-run the screening on defined triggers: promotion into a principal role, transfer into a fingerprintable function, a new criminal charge or regulatory action disclosed, or a customer complaint alleging dishonesty.
Confirm a fingerprint is on file covering the new function; submit a fresh one where the person was previously out of scope.
Re-test statutory disqualification and 1033 status on any new criminal disposition and file the U4 amendment within 30 days of learning of it.
Record the trigger, the re-screen scope and the conclusion on the person's file.
checklist.done: each trigger event has a recorded re-screen with a fresh disqualification conclusion and, where needed, a U4 amendment inside 30 days.

checklist.step: Retain the screening record for the required periods
actions: File per person: consents, fingerprint submission and result, CRD and public records extracts, verification evidence, the Rule 3110(e) memo, the disqualification memo and the U4, under REG-014-C15.
Apply the SEA Rule 17f-2(d) label to fingerprint records — at least 3 years after termination — and the 6-year FINRA Rule 4511 label to the investigation file.
Restrict access to the screening file to Compliance, HR and Counsel, and keep FCRA consumer reports in a segregated area.
Confirm the record is searchable by CRD number, national producer number and hire date, and record the retention expiry.
checklist.done: each screening file is complete, access-restricted, labelled to both retention rules and searchable by CRD number and hire date.

testing.step: Build the population of new associated persons for the quarter
actions: Extract from Workday every joiner and internal transfer in the quarter with start date, role and reporting line.
Extract from CRD every Form U4 filed in the quarter with the filing date and the registration categories requested.
Extract from the producer management system every new producer contract and appointment in the quarter.
Sign the extract with the run date and record row counts per source before sampling.
testing.done: a dated, signed population of joiners, U4 filings and new producer contracts exists with per-source row counts.

testing.step: Reconcile the population to the fingerprint submission log and CRD
actions: Match every U4 filed in the quarter to a fingerprint submission record and a returned result, and list every filing with neither.

Match every Workday joiner classified fingerprintable to a submission, and independently test the classification of 15 joiners classified out of scope against their actual duties and system entitlements.
List every person with securities or books-and-records entitlements in the IAM platform who has no fingerprint record — entitlement is evidence of function.
Resolve or log every difference before sampling and record the reconciled counts.
testing.done: every U4 and fingerprintable joiner reconciles to a submission and result, and entitlement-based misclassifications are identified.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample
actions: Take 100% of persons with any disclosure event, any FBI criminal history return, or any statutory disqualification review.
Take 30 further persons at random on a recorded seed, stratified across registered representatives, principals, non-registered fingerprintable staff and contracted producers.
Add 100% of persons who started before their fingerprint result returned.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers all disclosure cases and all early starts.

testing.step: Re-perform the CRD and public records search for each sampled person
actions: In FINRA Gateway pull the Individual Snapshot and Disclosure report for each sampled person as at the hire date and read the disclosures and prior U5 reasons yourself.
Compare to the questionnaire answers and to the U4 as filed; an undisclosed CRD disclosure is an exception regardless of the final decision.
Re-run a public records check on 10 sampled persons through the vendor and compare the scope and results to the file copy.
Capture the CRD disclosure page and the re-run report into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled person has an independent CRD re-performance and 10 have a re-run public records comparison, both captured.

testing.step: Test the fingerprint submission, result and pre-start position
actions: For each sampled person read the fingerprint submission date, the transaction control number and the returned FBI result date from CRD.
Compare the result date to the start date and to the date system entitlements to securities or books-and-records systems were granted in the IAM platform.
Where the person started first, confirm the written restriction existed and that IAM shows no in-scope entitlement during the restriction period.
Test rejected prints: confirm the resubmission was immediate and that a second rejection routed to the name-check alternative.
testing.done: every sampled person's fingerprint clearance is proven to precede their entitlements, or the restriction is evidenced in IAM.

testing.step: Re-perform the employment and residence verification on a sub-sample
actions: Take 10 sampled persons and re-contact one prior employer each, recording the contact name, date, employment dates and reason for leaving.
Compare to the file record and to the U4 employment history and list every difference in dates or reason.
Test the 10-year residence trail against the public records address history and flag any undisclosed address.
Treat a verification recorded with no contact name and date as unperformed.
testing.done: 10 sampled verifications are independently re-performed with contact evidence and compared to the file and the U4.

testing.step: Test the statutory disqualification and 1033 conclusions
actions: Read each sampled disqualification memo against Exchange Act 3(a)(39) and FINRA By-Laws Article III Section 3(b) as they read at the decision date, limb by limb.
Confirm the insurance-side 18 U.S.C. 1033 analysis was performed separately and that any required state written consent was obtained before insurance activity began.
Where an MC-400 was required, confirm it was filed and approved before the person acted in a registered capacity.
Confirm every signed 1033 consent is on file for persons engaged in the business of insurance.
testing.done: every sampled disqualification conclusion is limb-tested on both the securities and insurance sides with the required consents evidenced.

testing.step: Recompute the 30-day investigation clock and the U5 review window
actions: Recompute Rule 3110(e) memo signature date minus U4 filing date for every sampled person and test against 30 calendar days.
Recompute the date the prior firm's Form U5 was reviewed minus the U4 filing date and test against the 60-day requirement for applicants registered elsewhere in the last 5 years.
Recompute fingerprint submission date minus start date and list every negative result.
Compute the quarter's rate of investigations completed beyond 30 days and compare it to the zero-tolerance standard.
testing.done: the 30-day and 60-day clocks are independently recomputed for every sampled person and every breach is listed and quantified.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the person, the CRD number, the control that failed, the day count and the rule breached.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: role misclassified as out of scope, fingerprint submitted after start, rejection not resubmitted, verification not evidenced, U4 filed before reconciliation, 1033 consent missing.
Assign an owner and a remediation date and, where a person performed fingerprintable functions before clearance, suspend entitlements the same day and open a Rule 4530 self-report assessment.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue reference, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the count of persons who acted before clearance and of late Rule 3110(e) investigations to the zero-tolerance thresholds.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the workpaper references and any self-report opened.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Compliance Operations and HR and approved no sampled screening, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Audit and Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the pre-clearance count and the late-investigation count, and is filed with a reporting date.

Accountable obligation owner.value: Owns the quarterly reconciliation of the producer and registered-person roster to CRD and to state appointment records, and owns the preservation of the resulting records under the FINRA and Exchange Act retention rules

Citation verified against current regula.value: Yes — FINRA Rule 4511 (General Requirements) read with SEA Rule 17a-3 for the records to be made and SEA Rule 17a-4 for the periods and formats, reconciling the FINRA default of 6 years where no SEC period is specified against the SEC periods where they differ; FINRA By-Laws Article V for the U4/U5 record trail

In-scope processes.value: Quarterly three-way reconciliation of the internal producer roster to the CRD registered-person record and to the state appointment records held in the NIPR Producer Database, and the preservation of the roster, reconciliation and supporting licensing records for their required periods

In-scope systems.value: Producer roster and reconciliation output held in the producer management system; state appointments read from the NIPR Producer Database; registrations read from CRD; the preserved record set held in the document management repository in WORM-compliant storage

Compliance procedure documented.value: Producer Roster Reconciliation and Records Preservation Procedure — the three-source extract definition, the match keys, the break categories and their owners, the correction routes, and the retention schedule mapping each record type to its FINRA and SEC period and format

Compliance procedure approved.value: Approved by the Head of Compliance with the Records Manager as co-owner of the retention schedule; re-approved annually and on any change to SEA Rule 17a-4 or the firm's storage arrangements

Filing/reporting deadlines tracked.value: Reconciliation run within 10 business days of each quarter end and breaks cleared within 30 days; the electronic storage undertaking and the third-party access letter filed with FINRA before any new storage system is used; records produced to a regulator within the period specified in the request, normally within the 5-business-day internal service standard

Deadline reminders configured.value: Producer system calendar alerts on quarter-end plus 5 and plus 10 business days for the reconciliation run, and per-break alerts at day 15, 25 and 29 of the 30-day clearance window; an annual alert on the retention schedule review date

Evidence retained per the retention requ.value: Reconciliation extracts, break register and clearance evidence retained 6 years with the first 2 years in an easily accessible place per FINRA Rule 4511(b) and SEA Rule 17a-4(b); U4 and U5 records and licensing files retained 3 years after termination per SEA Rule 17a-4(e)(1), stored in a non-rewriteable, non-erasable format with the required audit trail

Violations/exceptions logged with dispos.value: Every unresolved reconciliation break past 30 days, every roster record with no supporting licensing document and every record found outside its required format or period is logged with the producer number, the break category, the owner and a dated remediation plan

Remediation sign-off captured.value: Signs the quarterly reconciliation certificate confirming all breaks are cleared or owned, and signs off any records-preservation gap before the quarter closes

Test population (in-scope transactions,.value: The quarter's three source extracts — the internal producer roster, the CRD registered-person record and the NIPR state appointment record — together with the break register and the retention schedule applied to the resulting record set

Pass/fail thresholds.value: Zero tolerance on an active producer writing business in a state where the appointment record shows no appointment; the reconciliation fails if any break remains uncleared and unowned after 30 days, or if any record type is stored outside its required period or format

Compliance test frequency matched to the.value: The reconciliation is quarterly and is tested each quarter on the completed run; the retention and format testing runs annually across every record type in the schedule

Independent reviewer (segregated from th.value: Reviewer must not sit in Licensing Operations and must not have performed the reconciliation or cleared any sampled break

Evidence location for test results.value: Quarterly roster reconciliation and records preservation workpaper (three-source extracts, match re-performance, break ageing, retention schedule test, exception log) in the compliance evidence repository under REG-014-C16

Regulator-ready documentation.value: Signed quarterly reconciliation certificate with the three source extracts and the cleared break register, plus the retention schedule and the storage undertaking, producible for a state market conduct exam or a FINRA books-and-records review within 5 business days

Regulator response path.value: Producer Compliance Manager answers state appointment record inquiries; the Records Manager handles books-and-records production requests and Regulatory Counsel clears any admission of an unappointed writing producer or an unpreserved record

checklist.step: Define the three source extracts and freeze the as-at date
actions: Fix the as-at date at the quarter end and run all three extracts against that date so a mid-run change cannot create a phantom break.
Extract the internal roster: national producer number, CRD number, tax identification number, status, appointed states, product authorities, agency hierarchy and contract dates.
Extract from CRD the registered-person record: CRD number, registration categories, registration states and status dates.
Extract from the NIPR Producer Database the state appointment record for every appointing company by NAIC code, with appointment effective and termination dates.
Record the row count and the run timestamp of each extract on the reconciliation cover sheet.
checklist.done: three extracts run against a single frozen as-at date, each with a recorded row count and run timestamp.

checklist.step: Match the three sources on the agreed keys
actions: Match internal roster to NIPR on national producer number plus state plus appointing company NAIC code — never on name, which breaks on marriages and suffixes.
Match internal roster to CRD on CRD number plus registration state.
Normalise the state and company codes before matching and log any record with a missing key as an unmatched item rather than dropping it.
Output four result sets: matched, in roster only, in NIPR only, and in CRD only, with counts that sum back to the extract totals.
checklist.done: the match produces four result sets whose counts reconcile back to the three extract row counts.

checklist.step: Categorise every break
actions: Assign each break a category: appointment missing at the state, appointment held for a terminated producer, roster state missing for a held appointment, registration lapsed with appointment live, licence expired with appointment live, or key data mismatch.
Rank the categories by risk — a producer writing business with no state appointment sits at the top and is worked the same day.
Assign a named owner per category: Licensing Operations for filing breaks, Distribution Operations for contract-status breaks, Data Quality for key mismatches.
Load every break into the break register with its as-at date so ageing runs from the reconciliation, not from the day someone noticed.
checklist.done: every break carries a category, a risk rank, a named owner and an ageing clock started at the as-at date.

checklist.step: Test each break against actual written business
actions: For every missing-appointment break extract applications signed and policies issued by that producer in that state since the contract date.
Read the application images to confirm the signed dates rather than trusting the keyed field.
Quantify premium, policy count and commission paid for each break with business attached and escalate it to the Head of Compliance the same day.
Mark breaks with no business attached as administrative so effort concentrates where customers are affected.
checklist.done: every missing-appointment break is classified as business-affecting or administrative, with premium and policy counts quantified.

checklist.step: Clear the appointment and termination filing breaks through NIPR
actions: For missing appointments, submit the appointment transaction in the NIPR Gateway with the correct company NAIC code and lines of authority and pay the state fee, noting that a back-dated effective date is generally not available.
For appointments held on terminated producers, submit the termination with the correct reason code and the actual termination date.
Read each transaction response the same day and re-work rejections rather than letting them age into the next quarter.
Post the confirmation number and the new effective or termination date back to the break register and to the producer record.
checklist.done: every filing break is cleared with a NIPR confirmation number posted to the break register and the producer record.

checklist.step: Clear the CRD registration breaks
actions: For registrations that lapsed while the appointment is live, establish whether the person is still active — if so file the registration request or the renewal, and if not file the Form U5.
For persons registered in CRD but absent from the roster, confirm with HR and Distribution whether they are still associated and correct whichever source is wrong.
File any required U4 amendment within 30 days of learning of the underlying change.
Record the CRD acknowledgement and the corrected status on the break register.
checklist.done: every CRD break is cleared by a filed registration, renewal, U5 or roster correction with an acknowledgement recorded.

checklist.step: Fix the data-quality breaks at source
actions: For each key mismatch establish which system holds the authoritative value — NIPR for the national producer number, CRD for the CRD number, HRIS for employment status.
Correct the non-authoritative system and record the correction with the source and the date, rather than overwriting both sides to agree.
Add a validation rule at the point of entry so the same mismatch cannot recur — for example rejecting a producer record without a national producer number.
Report recurring mismatch patterns to the Producer Compliance Manager for a process fix rather than a quarterly cleanup.
checklist.done: each data break is corrected in the non-authoritative system with a validation rule added to prevent recurrence.

checklist.step: Age and escalate uncleared breaks
actions: Run the break ageing report weekly showing days open from the as-at date against the 30-day clearance standard.
Escalate business-affecting breaks to the Head of Compliance immediately and all breaks at day 25 with the owner named.
Refuse to close any break on an assertion — close only on a NIPR confirmation, a CRD acknowledgement or a corrected system record.
Carry breaks not cleared in 30 days into the next quarter's register with their original as-at date so the ageing is not reset.
checklist.done: no break is closed without system evidence and every break over 25 days is escalated with its owner named.

checklist.step: Sign the quarterly reconciliation certificate
actions: Read the reconciliation cover sheet: extract counts, match result counts, break counts by category, breaks cleared and breaks carried forward with owners.
Confirm every business-affecting break has a quantified impact and a counsel decision where business was written without appointment.
Sign and date the certificate stating the as-at date and the position on carried-forward breaks.
Table the certificate at the Compliance Committee with the trend in break counts by category.
checklist.done: a signed, dated reconciliation certificate states the as-at date, the break position and the carried-forward owners.

checklist.step: Map every record type to its retention period and format
actions: List each record type this obligation produces: roster extracts, reconciliation cover sheets, break registers, NIPR confirmations, U4 and U5 filings, licensing correspondence and commission records.

Assign each the FINRA Rule 4511 default of 6 years where no SEC period applies, and the specific SEA Rule 17a-4 period where one does — 3 years after termination for U4 and U5 records under 17a-4(e)(1), 6 years for records under 17a-3(a)(1) to (3).
Record for each type where the first 2 years are held in an easily accessible place, as Rule 4511(b) requires.
Have Regulatory Counsel review the schedule annually and record the review date.
checklist.done: every record type carries a documented period, the governing rule and the location of its easily accessible copy.

checklist.step: Prove the storage format meets the electronic records rule
actions: Confirm the repository stores the record set in a non-rewriteable, non-erasable format or under the audit-trail alternative permitted by SEA Rule 17a-4(f), and obtain the vendor attestation.
Confirm a duplicate copy is stored separately from the original for the same period and test that it is readable.
Confirm the required undertaking from the third-party access person is on file with FINRA, naming someone able to furnish records to the regulator independently of the firm.
Confirm the index permits retrieval of any record by producer number, record type and date, and that legible copies can be produced.
checklist.done: the storage arrangement is evidenced as rule-compliant with a duplicate copy, a filed third-party undertaking and a working index.

checklist.step: Test retrieval against a live production request standard
actions: Each quarter pick 10 records at random across types and ages and ask a colleague to retrieve them without help.
Time each retrieval against the 5-business-day service standard and note anything that required a restore from archive.
Confirm each retrieved record is legible, complete and carries its audit trail.
Log failures as records-preservation exceptions rather than as retrieval inconvenience.
checklist.done: a quarterly retrieval test on 10 records records the time, legibility and completeness of each, with failures logged as exceptions.

checklist.step: Apply and release legal holds correctly
actions: Apply a legal hold to the producer's full record set on notice of any litigation, arbitration, state inquiry or FINRA Rule 8210 request naming them.
Suspend the retention clock for held records and confirm the repository blocks disposition while the hold stands.
Release the hold only on written confirmation from Litigation Counsel and record the release date and approver.
Reconcile the hold list to the open matter list each quarter so a closed matter does not leave records held indefinitely.
checklist.done: every open matter has a matching legal hold with disposition blocked, and released holds carry a dated counsel approval.

checklist.step: Dispose of records only at the end of their period
actions: Run the disposition due-list quarterly showing records past their retention period and not under legal hold.
Have the Producer Compliance Manager confirm no open exception or inquiry touches the records before disposition proceeds.
Execute disposition and record a certificate of destruction naming the record types, the volumes and the date.
Never dispose of a record type whose period is measured from termination while the person remains associated.
checklist.done: disposition runs only on a confirmed due-list free of holds and open exceptions, evidenced by a certificate of destruction.

checklist.step: File the reconciliation and preservation evidence
actions: File the three source extracts, the match output, the break register with clearance evidence and the signed certificate under REG-014-C16 and the quarter.
Apply the 6-year label with the first 2 years in the easily accessible tier per FINRA Rule 4511(b).
Confirm the record is searchable by as-at date, national producer number, state and break category.
Record the retention expiry on the index entry.
checklist.done: each quarter's reconciliation evidence is filed, labelled for 6-year retention and searchable by as-at date, producer and state.

testing.step: Rebuild the three source extracts independently
actions: Re-run the internal roster extract from the producer management system at the same frozen as-at date and compare the row count to the reconciliation cover sheet.
Pull the state appointment record independently from the NIPR Producer Database for each appointing company NAIC code.
Pull the CRD registered-person record independently from FINRA Gateway.
Sign the rebuilt extracts with the run date and compare each row count to the counts recorded by the performer.
testing.done: three independently rebuilt extracts exist at the same as-at date with row counts compared to the performer's cover sheet.

testing.step: Reconcile the rebuilt extracts to the performer's match output
actions: Re-run the match on the agreed keys — national producer number plus state plus NAIC code, and CRD number plus state — and produce your own four result sets.
Compare your break count by category to the performer's break register and investigate every difference.
Confirm the performer's result counts sum back to their extract totals; a match output that does not reconcile hides dropped records.
List any record dropped for a missing key as an exception rather than a technical exclusion.
testing.done: an independently re-run match reconciles to the performer's break register or every difference is investigated and listed.

testing.step: Draw a documented, reproducible sample of breaks and matched records
actions: Take 100% of business-affecting breaks and 100% of breaks carried forward from a prior quarter.
Take 30 breaks at random from the remaining register on a recorded seed, stratified across the break categories.
Take 20 records the performer classified as matched, to test for false matches where a name-based fallback was used.
Record the seed, population size, strata and selection date so the sample can be re-drawn identically.
testing.done: the sample is reproducible from the recorded seed and covers all business-affecting and carried-forward breaks plus matched records.

testing.step: Re-perform the appointment status check in the Producer Database
actions: For each sampled record run a Producer Database inquiry and read the appointment history per state for the appointing company: effective date, termination date and lines of authority.
Confirm the appointment status the performer recorded matches the PDB history as at the frozen date, not as at today.
For sampled matched records confirm the appointment genuinely covers the lines of authority the producer writes — a life appointment does not cover variable annuity business.
Capture the PDB appointment history screen for each sampled record into the workpaper.
testing.done: each sampled record's appointment status and lines of authority are independently proven from PDB history and captured.

testing.step: Trace business-affecting breaks to source application images
actions: For every business-affecting break extract the applications and policies attributed to that producer in that state within the unappointed period.
Open the application images and read the signed dates and the writing producer number from the document rather than the keyed record.
Recompute premium, policy count and commission paid inside the unappointed window and compare to the performer's quantification.
Confirm each case reached the Head of Compliance and Regulatory Counsel with a recorded decision on state notification and commission treatment.
testing.done: every business-affecting break is independently quantified from source images with the counsel decision evidenced.

testing.step: Verify break clearances rest on system evidence
actions: For each sampled cleared break open the recorded NIPR confirmation number or CRD acknowledgement and confirm it exists and matches the state, company and date claimed.
Confirm the clearance date is after the break was raised — a clearance recorded before the as-at date indicates a mis-keyed register.
Treat any break closed with a comment but no confirmation reference as still open.
Re-check that data-quality clearances corrected the non-authoritative system, not both sides.
testing.done: every sampled clearance is supported by a verified confirmation reference and a plausible clearance date, or is reopened.

testing.step: Recompute break ageing against the 30-day standard
actions: Recompute days open for every break as clearance date, or test date if open, minus the frozen as-at date.
Test that carried-forward breaks kept their original as-at date rather than being re-dated at the new quarter.
Compute the proportion of breaks cleared inside 30 days and the count still open and unowned.
Recompute the reconciliation run date against the quarter-end plus 10-business-day standard.
testing.done: break ageing and the run date are independently recomputed and any re-dated carry-forward is identified.

testing.step: Test the retention schedule, storage format and retrieval
actions: Take one record of each type in the schedule and confirm the applied retention label matches the rule cited — 6 years under FINRA Rule 4511 or the specific SEA Rule 17a-4 period.
Confirm records under 3 years old are held in the easily accessible tier and that the duplicate copy exists and opens.
Confirm the third-party access undertaking on file with FINRA names a current individual, not a departed employee.
Request 10 records cold and time the retrieval against the 5-business-day standard, checking legibility and audit trail.
Test that a record under legal hold cannot be disposed of by attempting a disposition in a test environment.
testing.done: every record type's period, tier, duplicate, undertaking and retrievability is independently tested, including a hold-blocking test.

testing.step: Log every exception with root cause, owner and remediation date
actions: Raise a GRC issue per exception naming the producer number, the state, the break category or record type and the rule breached.

Assign a root cause from the fixed list: extract not run at the frozen date, match fell back to name, break closed without confirmation, carry-forward re-dated, retention period wrong, duplicate copy missing, undertaking names a leaver.
Assign an owner and a remediation date, and route any business written without appointment to Regulatory Counsel for a state notification decision within 5 business days.
Carry every open exception into the next quarter's test as a mandatory retest row.
testing.done: every exception has an issue reference, a root cause from the fixed list, an owner, a remediation date and a retest commitment.

testing.step: Conclude, obtain independent sign-off and report
actions: Compare the count of unappointed writing producers and of breaks open past 30 days to the zero-tolerance thresholds, and state the retention test result by record type.
Write the conclusion — effective, effective with exceptions, or ineffective — naming the workpaper references behind it.
Have the independent reviewer, who sits outside Licensing Operations and cleared no sampled break, sign and date the workpaper.
Report to the Compliance Committee at its next sitting and file the signed workpaper in the compliance evidence repository.
testing.done: a signed workpaper states the conclusion, the unappointed-writing count, the break ageing position and the retention test result.
